anchors:
- Root: ن-ظ-ر (na-ẓa-ra)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To look, to consider, to examine with deliberation; intellectual scrutiny of a matter.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Contemplative examination (naẓar) leading to juridical or theological judgment; the act of weighing evidence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical sight; Metaphorical: reflective inquiry (taʾammul) into a ruling's validity.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Exceptional Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The phrase "after he administers the oath to him, there is consideration therein" employs a temporal clause followed by a suspended judgment, requiring the reader to parse the exception (istithnāʾ) as modifying the permissibility of the act.
translation:
I say — and God grants success:

Ibn ʿArafah said: "After he administers the oath to him, there is consideration therein (naẓar) — whether that [oath] is, in their religious community, a thing deemed abominable (mubāḥḥan)."

And consider also, from what Mālik explicitly stipulated, the fear that one might suppose it disliked (karāhah) for a person in a state of minor impurity (ḥadath) to recite the Qur'an. He — Mālik — devoted a chapter heading to this in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, saying: "The concession (rukhṣah) regarding the recitation of the Qur'an without ablution (wuḍūʾ)." Mālik relates from Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, from Ibn Sīrīn, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was among a people who were reciting [the Qur'an] — consider his chapter heading. [The chain continues:] Ibn Farḥūn — al-Dībāj al-Mudhhab: 62–67; al-Ṣafadī — al-Wāfī bi-l-Wafayāt 6/233; Ibn Taghrī Birdī — al-Manhal al-Ṣāfī: 1/234–233, ed. Dr. Muḥammad Muḥammad Amīn, al-Hayʾah al-Miṣriyyah al-ʿĀmmah li-l-Kitāb, 1984; Ibn al-Qāḍī — Durrat al-Ḥijāl: 1/8; and Makhlūf — Shajarat al-Nūr al-Zakiyyah: 188–189. [Regarding] Ibn ʿĀt (512–582 AH / 1118–1186 CE), Hārūn ibn Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn ʿĀt, Abū Muḥammad al-Tafarshi al-Shāṭibī: a jurist among the Mālikī jurists. He was appointed judge in Shāṭibah and his conduct was praised. Among his works is "al-Ṭurar al-Mawḍūʿah ʿalā al-Wathāʾiq al-Majmūʿah." See: al-Naẓar, al-Marqabah al-ʿUlyā li-l-Bāhī: 116; al-Takmilah by Ibn al-Abbār: 1/101–102; al-Takmilah by al-Mundhirī: biography no. 1232; Tārīkh al-Islām: 14/1/18–345; Tadhkirat al-Ḥuffāẓ: 4/1289–1390; al-ʿIbar: 5/31; and Shadharāt al-Dhahab: 5/36–37.

(2) Ibn ʿArafah al-Tūnisī (716–803 AH / 1316–1400 CE): Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafah al-Warghamī, the Imām of Tunis, its khaṭīb, its muftī, and its greatest scholar. He began delivering the khuṭbah in 772 AH and issuing fatwās in 773 AH. He was a leading figure among the heads of the Mālikī school; he taught at the Great Mosque of Tunis. Among his books: al-Mabsūṭ fī al-Fiqh and al-Ḥudūd fī Muṣṭalaḥāt al-Fiqh. See: al-Ḍawʾ al-Lāmiʿ 9:240–242; Bughyat al-Wuʿāh 98:99; al-Dībāj 337–340.

(3) He is the Imām Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī, Abū Bakr ibn Abī Tamīmah Kaysān al-ʿAnazī: trustworthy, established, an authority (ḥujjah). He was born in the year 66 AH and died in 131 AH. Ṭabaqāt Ibn Saʿd 7/246; al-Ansāb 3/255; Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ 5/516.

(4) He is Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn, the Imām, the ascetic (al-rāhbānī), Abū Bakr, the freed slave of Anas ibn Mālik — may God be pleased with him. He was an Imām of abundant knowledge, a master of dream interpretation (taʿbīr), and a leader in scrupulous piety (waraʿ). He saw thirty of the Companions of the Prophet — peace be upon him. [The narration continues:] ʿUmar went to relieve himself, then returned while reciting the Qur'an. A man said to him: "O Commander of the Believers, do you recite the Qur'an while not in a state of ablution?" ʿUmar replied: "Who gave you this fatwā? Musaylimah?"

Al-Bājī said: "There is no disagreement that minor impurity (al-ḥadath al-aṣghar) does not prevent recitation." And Abū ʿUmar said: "The Messenger of God — peace be upon him — used to say: 'Nothing veils him from the recitation of the Qur'an except janābah (major impurity)...'" — the ḥadīth. And the people of knowledge do not differ on this, except for one who deviates from their consensus (jamāʿah), one who is refuted by them.

And Abū Dāwūd and others transmitted that the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — said: "Recite 'Yā Sīn' at the time of your dying." Consider: if a ḥadīth from the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — had come contrary to this, why would it not be like reclining [i.e., permissible without ablution]?

And consider also, from this same method, the explicit statement of al-Shāṭibī on its permissibility and that it is excepted from an originally prohibited principle: the evidentiary use of dreams (al-istidlāl bi-l-ruʾyā). He said: "He errs who uses a dream as evidence for any one of the [legal] acts; for the dream of other than the prophets is not made a basis for a legal ruling (ḥukm sharʿī) in any case — unless one presents it against what we possess of the legal rulings; if those rulings permit it, one acts in accordance with it." As is related of al-Kattānī: "I saw the Prophet — peace be upon him — in a dream, and I said: 'O Messenger of God, pray to God that He not cause my heart to die.' He said: 'Say: O Living, O Self-Subsistent, there is no god but You.'" He said: "This is good speech, with no problem in its soundness." Even though Ibn Rushd said: "It is not permissible to use a dream as evidence for a legal ruling."

And consider also what al-Shāṭibī explicitly stated regarding its permissibility and his strengthening of the permissibility — lest one suppose that this is among the things concerning which the Messenger of God — peace be upon him — died [without clarification]. He died in the year 10 AH. See: Ṭabaqāt ʿUlamāʾ al-Ḥadīth 1/151–152; Siyar Aʿlām al-Nubalāʾ 6/64.

(5) He is the ḥāfiẓ, the authority (al-ʿallāmah), Sulaymān ibn Khalaf ibn Saʿd al-Tujībī al-Mālikī al-Andalusī al-Bājī. He was among the greatest scholars of al-Andalus and its preservers of ḥadīth. He traveled to the East in the year 426 AH, then returned to his homeland after thirteen years with vast knowledge. He was appointed judge in various places and authored numerous works. See: al-Tadhkirah 3/1178; and consider also his biography in Muʿjam al-Udabāʾ 11/206–251; al-Aʿyān 2/209; and Ibn Abī Shaybah (3/273), and al-Nasāʾī in ʿAmal al-Yawm wa-l-Laylah, no. (1074), and Aḥmad (5/26–27).

title_en: The Conduct of the Rightly Guided in the Stations of Religion — Section 9: On the Permissibility of Devotional Poetry, Supplication After Prayers, and the Limits of Innovation (Bidʿah)
arabic_text:
منهج اللي الام النابع: الأغلبالجمة في الدين ينبغي مثل الإمام الذي التزم شعرًا ينشده دبر كل صلاة قال الشاطبي؛ إن قوما أنوا عمر بن الخطاب» فقالوا له يا أمير المؤمنين: إن لنا إماما إذا فرغ من صلاته تغنى» فقال له عمر: ويحك؛ بلغني عنك أمر ساءني؛ فقال له: وما هويا أمير المؤمنين» فإني أعيتك من نفسي؟ قال: فإنه بلغني أنك إذا صليت تغنيت؛ قال: نعم؛ يا أمير المؤمنين, قال: أوتتمجن في عبادتك؟ قال: لاء يا أمير المؤمنين؛ ولكنها عظة أعظ بها نفسي؛ قال عمر: فقلهاء فإن كان كلاما حسنًا قلته معك؛ وإن كان قبيحًا نهيتك عنهه فأنشده أبياناه منها: نفس لا كنت ولا كان الهوى راقبي المولى وخافي وارهبي فقال عمر رضي الله عنه: نفس لا كنت ولا كان الهسوى راقبي المسولى وخصاقي وارهبي ثم قال عمر رضي الله عنه: على هذا فليغن من غنى. ثم رشح الشاطبي جواز هذا قائلا: فتأملوا قوله: بلغني عنك أمر ساءني؛ مع قوله: أوتشمجن في عبادنك. فهي من أشد ما يكون في الإنكار حتى أعلمه أنه يردد على لسانه أييات حكمة فيها عظة؛ فحيتشذ أقره وسلم له أحسن من هذاء قال الشاطبي: وهذا كان فمل القوم؛ قال: وهم مع ذلك لم يقتصروا في التنشيط للتفوس ولا الوعظ على مجرد الشعرء بل وعظوا أنفسهم بكل موعظة. اه نص الشاطبي.

وانظر أيضًا تنبيهه على ما توهم أنه يلزمه أنه يكرهه لما ذكر مذهبه في الدعاء أدبار الصلوات؛ قال: لو فرضنا الدعاء بالهيئة الاجتماعية وقع من أئمة الصلاة في المساجد في بعض الأوقات؛ لكان جائرًا كما دعا رسول الله يق دعاء الاستسقاء على هيئة الاجتماع؛ قال: وكان عمر إذا صلى العشاء أخرج الناس من المسجد فتخلف ليلة مع قوم يذكرون اله فأتى إليهم؛ فعرفهم؛ وجلس معهم؛ فجعل يقولة يا فلان: ادع الله لناء يا فلان. ادع الله لناء حتى صار الدعاء إلى عمر فكانوا يقولون: عمر فظ غليظ؛ فلم أر أحدًا من الناس تلك الساعة أرق من عمرء لا تكلى؛ ولا أحد من الناس.

وقال رجل لأنس يوما: يا أبا حمزة؛ لو دعوت الله لنا بدعوات؛ فقال: اللهم آثنا في الدنيا حسنة وفي الآخرة حسنة. وقنا عذاب النار؛ قال الشاطبي: فإذا كان الأمر على هذاء فلا إنكار فيه. اه وقد أكثرت من هذه المشل المنصوص على أنها جائزة منها: ما التزم دبر كل صلاة: كالغناء الذي ذكره الشاطبي؛ ومنها: ما النزم أربعين مرة في كل يوم لرؤيا ربت في النوم؛ كما ذكره الشاطبي أيضاء ومنها: ما فعل عمر عند الخروج من الخلاء على غير وضوء؛ ومنها: ما هو من الراحات أو العادات تنبا على أن من وقف عندها وعند ما يشبهها قصارى ما أقول: إنه ظالم لنفسه؛ إن لم أقل: إنه مقتصد؛ ولا أقول: إنه مبتدع أو ضالء بل إن فعل شيتًا من هذا قبل تسليمة التحليل من الفرض صحت صلاته عند أبي حتيفة؛ وإن فعلها بعد السلام وقبل تسليمة الرد صحت صلاته وفعل بدعة مذمومة؛ إذ حقيقة البدعة المذمومة حسب ما يأئي هي التي تميت السنة أو تكاد تفضي إلى إمانتهاء وإن فعلها بعد تسليمة الرد صحت صلاته بإجماع وفعل جائراء ثم أقول: إن ترك ذلك لما هو أرفع وخير مما تسرك فهو سابق بالخيرات؛ وإن تركهها لأخخس منها خوف آفة من خنارج يعمل بذلك ينا على الله عز وجل أن تعتفد العامة من أنا في الحي حتى أنسب؛ فهو كقول العامة: جائز بروحه؛ مضل لغيره» مستهزئ بنظرائه؛ مدخل على الناس شغًا في دينهم وحيرة في قلوبهم؛ وسوء ظن في مقلديهم؛ كما بأتي لشيخي ابن سراج رحمه الله لا سيما إن كان هذا المتروك من قبيل المشروع الذي لا يكون أبدا أحظ من المباح؛ ومن نذره لزمه؛ ولو أوصى بجزاء عليه لوجب تنفية مكروه: وقال بعضهمة إنه مستحبء أن فعل ذلك أفضل. قال عز الدين بن عبد السلام: وذلك كرفع اليدين» قال: وإنما قلنا هذا لأن الشرع يحتاط لفعل المندويات: كما يحتاط لقعل الواجيات.
anchors:
- Root: ن-ظ-م (na-ẓa-ma)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To string together, arrange in order; a composed poem (naẓm) as a structured sequence of words.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ordering of acts or words toward a coherent end; here, the deliberate commitment (iltizām) to a recited verse as a disciplined devotional practice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for physical stringing; metaphorical (majāz) for the soul's binding itself to a regular act of worship.
- Root: غ-ن-ي (gha-na-ya)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Singing, melodious recitation; also richness or self-sufficiency (ghinā).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Vocal modulation in recitation; in worship, distinguished from idle song (ghināʾ) by intent (niyyah) and content.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for musical chant; metaphorical for the heart's "enrichment" through admonition (mawʿiẓah).
- Root: ب-د-ع (ba-da-ʿa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To originate something new without prior example.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah, a novel practice; blameworthy bidʿah is that which kills a Sunnah or leads to its extinction, as the author will define.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for creation ex nihilo (divine); metaphorical for human innovation in religion, judged by its effect on established practice.
- Root: د-ع-و (da-ʿa-wa)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To call, invoke, supplicate.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Supplication (duʿāʾ) as the essence of worship; collective supplication (duʿāʾ bi-l-hayʾah al-ijtimāʿiyyah) has prophetic precedent (e.g., istisqāʾ).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for calling upon God; metaphorical for the soul's turning in need (iftiqār) to the Necessary Being.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa-l-istithnāʾ) — The author's repeated use of "in... fa-in..." (if... then...) and "illā an..." (unless...) structures the legal gradation (jāʾiz, makrūh, mandūb) with precise syntactic conditionality, mirroring juristic casuistry.
translation:
I say — and God grants success — the path of the rightly guided in matters of religion requires an imam like the one who committed himself to a poem he would recite after every prayer. Al-Shāṭibī related: A group of people came to ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb and said to him, "O Commander of the Believers, we have an imam who, when he finishes his prayer, sings." ʿUmar said to him, "Woe to you! A matter has reached me about you that displeased me." The man said, "What is it, O Commander of the Believers? For I have wearied you with my own self?" He said, "It has reached me that when you pray, you sing." He replied, "Yes, O Commander of the Believers." ʿUmar said, "Do you jest in your worship?" He said, "No, O Commander of the Believers; rather, it is an admonition (mawʿiẓah) with which I admonish my own soul." ʿUmar said, "Then say it — if it is good speech, I will say it with you; and if it is ugly, I will forbid you from it." So he recited to him two verses from it, including: "O soul, be not — and let not passion be — watchful of the Master, and fear, and be in awe." ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "O soul, be not — and let not passion be — watchful of the Master, and fear, and be in awe." Then ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, said: "On this let him sing who sings."

Then al-Shāṭibī endorsed the permissibility of this, saying: "Reflect on his words, 'A matter has reached me about you that displeased me,' along with his words, 'Do you jest in your worship?' — for this is among the severest forms of disapproval, until he informed him that he was repeating on his tongue verses of wisdom containing admonition. When he clarified this, he approved him and conceded to him — and nothing is better than this." Al-Shāṭibī said: "And this was the practice of the people (al-qawm)." He said: "Yet despite that, they did not restrict their stimulation of souls or their admonition to mere poetry; rather, they admonished themselves with every kind of admonition." End of al-Shāṭibī's text.

Consider also his warning regarding what one might imagine to be entailed — namely, that he disapproves of it — given his stated position on supplication after the prayers (adbār al-ṣalawāt). He said: "If we suppose supplication in the collective manner (al-hayʾah al-ijtimāʿiyyah) to occur from the prayer leaders in the mosques at certain times, it would be permissible, just as the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, supplicated in the prayer for rain (istisqāʾ) in the collective manner." He said: "And ʿUmar, when he prayed the night prayer (al-ʿishāʾ), would expel the people from the mosque. One night he lingered with a group who were remembering God, so he came to them, recognized them, and sat with them. He began saying, 'O so-and-so, supplicate God for us; O so-and-so, supplicate God for us,' until the supplication came around to ʿUmar. They would say, 'ʿUmar is harsh and stern' — yet I have never seen anyone among the people at that hour more tender-hearted than ʿUmar. No, not one among the people."

And a man said to Anas one day: "O Abā Ḥamzah, would you supplicate God for us with some supplications?" He said: "O God, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire." Al-Shāṭibī said: "So when the matter is thus, there is no disapproval in it." End.

I have multiplied these examples that are textually attested as permissible. Among them: what one commits to after every prayer — like the singing mentioned by al-Shāṭibī. Among them: what one commits to forty times each day for a vision seen in sleep, as al-Shāṭibī also mentioned. Among them: what ʿUmar did upon leaving the privy without ablution. Among them: what pertains to comforts (rāḥāt) or habits (ʿādāt). It follows that whoever stops at these and at what resembles them — the utmost I say is: he is unjust to himself (ẓālim li-nafsihi), if I do not say: he is moderate (muqtaṣid). I do not say: he is an innovator (mubtadiʿ) or misguided (ḍāll). Rather, if he does something of this sort before the first salutation of completion (taslīmat al-taḥlīl) from the obligatory prayer, his prayer is valid according to Abū Ḥanīfah. If he does it after the salutation and before the second salutation of response (taslīmat al-radd), his prayer is valid but he has committed a blameworthy innovation (bidʿah madhmūmah) — for the reality of blameworthy innovation, as will come, is that which kills a Sunnah or nearly leads to its extinction. And if he does it after the second salutation of response, his prayer is valid by consensus (ijmāʿ) and he has done a permissible act (jāʾiz).

Then I say: If one abandons this for something higher and better than what pleases you, then he is a forerunner in good deeds (sābiq bi-l-khayrāt). But if he abandons it for something inferior, fearing some external affliction, and acts thereby — then upon God, may He be exalted, it is incumbent that the common people (al-ʿāmmah) not believe that I am among the living such that I might be attributed — for it is like the common saying: "Permissible for himself, misleader of others" (jāʾiz bi-rūḥihi, muḍill li-ghayrihi); one who mocks his peers, who brings confusion into people's religion and bewilderment into their hearts, and ill suspicion toward their imitators (muqallidīn) — as will come from my teacher Ibn Sirāj, may God have mercy on him — especially if this abandoned thing is of the kind that is prescribed (mashrūʿ) and is never less than the permissible (mubāḥ). And whoever vows it, it becomes obligatory upon him; and if he bequeaths a recompense for it, executing it becomes obligatory, though disliked (makrūh). Some said it is recommended (mustaḥabb), and that doing it is more virtuous. ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām said: "That is like raising the hands [in prayer]." He said: "And we only say this because the Sacred Law is cautious in favor of performing the recommended acts (mandūbāt), just as it is cautious in favor of performing the obligatory acts (wājibāt)."

title_en: On the Limits of Enjoining Good and the Gravity of Rejecting Scholarly Disagreement
arabic_text:
وقال القرافي: ولأن القائل بالشرعية مثبت لأمر لم يطلع عليه النافي» والمثبت منهج اللي الام النابع: الأغلبالجمة في الدين 4 مقدم؛ قال: كتعارض البيتتين؛ وقال شيخ الشيوخ ابن لب”': إذا كان عمل الناس على قول لبعض العلماء؛ فلا ينبغي إنكاره؛ لا سيما إن كان الخلاف في كراهية والأفضل القيام بالمشروع والمسارعة إلى فعله؛ ولا يعارض ذلك بما عسى أن يعتقفده جاهل بسبب جهله. في الوضوء والصلاة والنصيام وسائر الوظائف المشروعة فضائل يقام بهاء ويثابر عليهاء ولم يقل أحد بتركها مخافة اعتقاد الوجوب بها. قال: وقد أشكل على الناس كلام مالك في مخالفة هذا الأصل في صيام ست من شوال؛ واختلفوا في توجيه قوله؛ فكيف يستقيم لأحد أن يقيس على هذا غيره.

ثم قال: فهذا جهالة عظيمة: ما حمل من أنكره على إتكاره إلا أنه أبصر ما أمامه: ولم يلتفت إلى ما خلف وراءه؛ وقف على بعض مسائل في المذهب لم يهتد الواضح سبيلهاء ولا شعر بوجهها ودليلهاء ولا علم اختلاف العلماء في أصلهاء ولم يعطها من الفهم والتأمل حقهاء ورأى أن العمل بخلاف ما انتهى إليه فهمه فيهاء. فظن أن لا علم إلا ما علم؛ ولا فهم إلا دون ما فهم؛ استحقر العامة؛ وجهل الخاصة؛ ورأى أنه وحده على الجادة؛ وصار في قيامه على الناس بالتكيرء كما قيل: إنباض بغير توتيرء وحاد ليس له بعير. اه بعض كلام شيخ الشيوخ ابن لب.

وهذا تكلم عليه أيضًا مفتي تونس البرزلي" في المنكر الدعاء أدبار الصلوات ونحو ذلك؛ قائلا: لم تسر بسيرة السلف في أن الأمر بالمعروف يكون بمعروقه قال سبحاته: لمََاُوَاين 4 [طه: 44]» وهذا إذا كان المأمور به واجببا بإجماع (ا ابن لت (01 - 782ه- 1301 - 1380م أبو سعيد فرج بن قاسم بن أحمد بن لْت» ال الأندلسي الغرتاطي. فقيه مالكي مفسر أصولي» مقرئ» نحوي أديب؛ ناظم؛ متكلم. أخذ العلم عن أبي الحسن القيجاطي: وابن الفخار البيري وغيرهماء وقرأ عليه ابن بكر وابن سلمون وأبو عيد الله الهاشمي وغيرهم؛ وقد وصفه صاحب نيل الابتهاج؛ بأنه من أكابر علماء المذهب المتأخرين ومحققيهم؛ ممن له درجة الاختبار في الفتوى إلى التحفيق بالعلوم والفنود. عن كتبه: الفتاوى» شرح اللجمل للجاجي شرح تصريف التسهيل.

(2) أبو القاسم البرزلي 740 - 84م - 1339 - 1343م) أبو الفاسم بن أحمد بن المعتل البلوي» القبرواني؛ التونسي؛ المالكي؛ الشير بالبرزلي؛ ققبه؛ ولد في حدود سنة 740 ورحل إلى القاهرة؛ وصار إماما بازيتونة؛ وأفتى ووعظ وتوفي بتونس. من آثاره: لديوان الكير في الفقهء النوازل: والقتاوى.

6“ متيج اللي) المقام الناسع: الأعل بالجذ في الدين أو المنهي عنه محرمًا بإجماع؛ وأنت قد عمدت إلى مستحب جائز الترك: أو مكروه جائز الفعل؛ أو مباح وغيره خير منهه وجل ذلك أو كله مختلف فيه.

اثم ذكر عن هذا الذي هو يتحدث معه أنه كبر هذه الأشياء وصيرها مناكير. قال: وقصاراها الاستحباب أو الكراهة أو الإباحة على اختلاف فيها أو في بعضهاء تركت أو قعلت لموجب قابل للاستحباب أو الكراهة أو الإباحة؛ وأخخذ فيها بغير مذهب مالك المرجح؛ وجرى عليه عمل الناس من غير تكير. وسيأتي أن أمر الحسبة ليس بالهوّنا. انظر النصوص الصريحة بالنهي في القرآن والسنة في مثل هذه الأموره أعني: مما هو وارد على ما في ملك الإنسان أنه نهي أدب أو إرشاد لاا نهي تحريمء حسب ما أبينه في المقام السادس؛ قصارى أمره إن لم يكن النهي عن فاضل لأفضل منه أنه مكروه؛ والمكروه من قييل الجائز.

وانظر فيما هو أعظم قول ابن شأس: لو رفع إلى قاض نكاح امرأة زوجت نفسها بغير ولي؛ فقال: لا أجيزه أن هذا ليس بحكم؛ قال الإمام ابن عرفة: مقتضى هذا أن لغيره بعده أن ينقضه؛ والظاهر أنه لا يجوز للشاني نقضه؛ لأن قول الأول: لا أجيزه حكم منه بأنه مكروه؛ والكراهة أحد أقسام الشرع الخمسة؛ يجب رعي كل حكم منها ولازمه؛ وحكم المكروه عدم نقضه بعد وقوعه.

قال ابن العربي: التوبة من المكروه مستحبة. وانظر إذا كانت الكراهة برك فاضل لأفضل؛ وربما يحتسب المحتسب؛ فيترك المحنسب عليه ما فيه فضل؛ ولا يترقى لأفضل.
anchors:
- Root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To disavow, to reject, to deem repugnant; the opposite of recognition (maʿrifah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Sharīʿah discourse, denotes declaring something outside the recognized norm (al-maʿrūf) — a legal-moral judgment, not mere personal distaste.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to fail to recognize. Metaphorical (majāz): to publicly censure an act as unlawful — a claim requiring proof.
- Root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Dislike, aversion; in legal taxonomy, the middle category between obligation and prohibition.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A divine ruling (ḥukm) rendering an act blameworthy but not punishable — one of the five legal categories.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: internal repugnance. Metaphorical: the jurisprudential rank of "disliked" (makrūh), which remains permissible in essence.
- Root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To reckon, to account; the office of the muḥtasib who enjoins right and forbids wrong.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The public function of vigilance over religious practice — requiring knowledge of consensus and disagreement.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: counting. Metaphorical: the moral reckoning one must apply to oneself before censuring others.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional restriction (taqyīd bi-l-sharṭ) — the permissibility of censure is conditioned upon the act being prohibited by consensus; where disagreement exists, the conditional clause fails and the ruling reverts to permissibility.
translation:
Al-Qarāfī said: "Because the one who affirms legal validity [of an act] affirms something the denier has not ascertained." The one who affirms follows the clearer path. The most preponderant view in religion is the foundational principle; he said: like the case of conflicting evidence [where the stronger is preferred]. And Shaykh al-Shuyūkh Ibn Lub said: "When the practice of the people follows the opinion of some scholars, it should not be denounced — especially when the disagreement concerns dislike (karāhah). And the superior course is to undertake what is legislated and hasten to perform it; nor should this be opposed by what an ignorant person might come to believe due to his ignorance. In ablution, prayer, fasting, and all the legislated devotions there are virtues by which one stands and perseveres, and no one has ever said to abandon them out of fear that someone might believe them obligatory." He said: "People found difficulty in Mālik's statement that contravenes this principle regarding fasting six days of Shawwāl, and they differed in interpreting his words — so how can anyone validly analogize other matters to this?"

Then he said: "This is great ignorance: nothing drove its denier to denial except that he saw only what was before him and paid no heed to what lay behind him. He stopped at certain issues in the school whose clear path he did not attain, whose aspect and proof he did not perceive, whose foundational disagreement among scholars he did not know, and to which he did not give their due of understanding and reflection. He saw that acting contrary to what his own understanding had reached was [wrong], so he fancied that there is no knowledge but what he knew, and no understanding but what he understood. He belittled the common folk, dismissed the elite, and deemed himself alone upon the straight path. He stood over the people with censure — as the saying goes: 'twanging without a bowstring, and a rider without a mount.'" This concludes some of the words of Shaykh al-Shuyūkh Ibn Lub.

And this was also addressed by the Muftī of Tunis, al-Burzulī, regarding the denunciation of supplication after the prescribed prayers and similar matters, saying: "He has not followed the path of the Salaf, that commanding good be done with goodness." He said, Exalted is He: {فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَّيِّنًا} [Ṭā-Hā: 44] — "And speak to him a gentle word." This applies when the commanded matter is obligatory by consensus. But you have taken a recommended act that may be omitted, or a disliked act that may be performed, or a permissible act beside which something else is better — and much or all of this is subject to disagreement.

Then he mentioned concerning this one with whom he was speaking that he magnified these matters and turned them into denounceable evils. He said: "Their utmost rank is recommendation, dislike, or permissibility — with disagreement concerning them or some of them. Whether abandoned or performed, it is for a reason admissible to recommendation, dislike, or permissibility. He acted in them according to other than the preponderant view of Mālik's school, while the practice of the people ran upon them without any denunciation." And it will come that the matter of ḥisbah is not trivial. Consider the explicit texts of prohibition in the Qur'an and Sunnah concerning such matters — I mean, what pertains to what is within a man's disposal as a prohibition of etiquette (adab) or guidance (irshād), not a prohibition of unlawfulness (taḥrīm) — as I shall clarify in the Sixth Station. The utmost of its matter, if the prohibition is not against a virtuous act for one more virtuous, is that it is disliked; and the disliked belongs to the category of the permissible.

And consider what is even greater — the saying of Ibn Shās: "If a judge were presented with the marriage of a woman who married herself without a guardian, and he said, 'I do not uphold it' — this is not a [final] judgment." Imām Ibn ʿArafah said: "The implication of this is that another judge after him may overturn it. But the apparent view is that the second may not overturn it, because the first's saying 'I do not uphold it' is a ruling from him that it is disliked; and dislike is one of the five legal categories, and every ruling and its necessary consequence must be observed. The ruling of the disliked is that it is not overturned after its occurrence."

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "Repentance from the disliked is recommended." And consider when the dislike is [due to] leaving a virtuous act for one more virtuous — perhaps the muḥtasib reckons, and the one reckoned against abandons what has virtue in it, and does not ascend to what is more virtuous.

title_en: On the Gravity of Abandoning Concessions and the Etiquette of Disagreement Among the Learned
arabic_text:
قال الشاطبي في "موافقاته": قد رأيت ترك الترخص في مواضع الترخص يوقع في مفسدة أو مفاسد يعظم موقعها شرعًاء فالناهي إذن عن مثل هذه الرخصة قد أمر بهذ المفسدة؛ إذ مذهب أهل السنة أن النهي عن الشيء الواحد أمر بضده أو بأحد أضداده إن كان ذا أضداد. قال بعضهم: رموا بهممهم إلى المراتب العالية: فلم يقدروا على الوصول إليها. قال أبو حامد: فتركوا التمييز: وهو عين الضلال ثم نقل من هذا المعنى؛ وقال: إن لم تكن إبل فمعزى.

.وقال ابن العربي: قلة الإئم بالنسية إلى كثرته خير كثير. وقال في "الإحيا. هكذا يتبغي أن تفهم حمد ما يحمد وذم ما يذم؛ وإلا جهلت قول القائل الصادقة منهج الندلي/ الفا اناسع: الأ بالجذ في الدين 7 حسنات الأبرار سيئات المقربين؛ وفال في موضع آخر: ومباحات العوام سيئات الأبرار. اه وسيأني لابن رشد وابن العربي أن على قوة الخلاف تقوي مراعاته.

وسياني في المقام السادس أن ما اختلف في مشروعيته أن فعله أولى؛ وأن بموت النبي فقي أمن أن يلحق بالفرائض ما ليس منها. وأن القرب إذا شهد الشرع باعتبار جنسها فهي مندوبة؛ زاد الشاطبي: وتؤخذ من المرائي في النوم؛ وسيأتي في المقام السادس أخيرًا أن النوافل ما قدر الشرع أن في فعله ثوابا من غير أن أمر به أو رغب فيه أو فعله. وسيأتي أن المساعدة فيما لا إثم فيه مندوبة: لعل أن تعناض بما ترك من الأفضل لأجل المساعدة ثواب المحسنين: والله سبحاته يقول: لمَاعلَ آلمُمييوت يبيل [التوبة: 91].

وسيأني أيضًا في آخر المقام السادس أن النهي إذا كان على ما في ملكك أنه نهي أدب وإرشاد. وقد يكون النهي عن فاضل لأفضل؛ كما يقال: يكره للقاعد في المسجد أن يترك القراءة والذكر؛ وللمجاور بمكة أن لا يحج كل عام وللمتزوج أن يعزله وعلى هذا حمل ابن رشد كراهة الوصية للذمي. وقال عياض: ما اختلف العلماء في تحليله وتحريمه؛ فلا يقال فيه: حرام؛ وقال في أول "الإكمال”: لا ينبغي اللآمر بالمعروف والناهي عن المتكر أن يحمل الناس على اجتهاده ومذهبه؛ وإنما منه ما اجتمع على إحدائه وإتككاره؛ ورشح محيي الدين النووي كلام عياض اقائلا: أما المختلف فيهء فلا إنكار فيه وليس للمفتي ولا للقاضي أن يعترض على من خالفه إذا لم يخالف نص القرآن والسنة والإجماع. وانظر في آخر المقام السادس من فتيا الشاطبي: إذا كان عمل الناس على قول مرجوح في النظر؛ فلا يعرض لهم ويجروا أنهم قلدوه في الزمان الأول» وجرى به العمل.

ومن "مقدمات" ابن رشد: ما اختلف العلماء في تحليله وتحريمه؛ فهو مكروه ومن تركه أجر؛ ومن فعله لا يأثم. وقال القرافي وعز الدين: من أتى شيئًا مختلفًا فيه يعتقد تحريمه أنكر عليه لانتهاكه الحرمة؛ وإن اعتقد تحليله لم يتكر عليه؛ إلا أن يكون مدرك المحلل ضعينًا ينقض الحكم بمثله في الشرع. وقال أبو عمر: ألاترى أن الصحابة اختلفوا وهم الأسوةء فلم يعب أحد منهم على صاحبه اجتهاد ولا وجد عليه في نفسه؟ إلى الله الشكوى؛ وهو المستعان على أمة نحن بين أظهرها 0 منهج اللي الما اناسع الأغل بالجذ في ادن تستحل الأعراض إذا خولفت. ونقل أبو عمر بسنده إلى الثوري''' قال: إذا رأيت الرجل يعمل بالعمل الذي اختلف فيه وأنت ترى غيره فلا تنهه.

وقد أمر المهدي” مالا أن يجمع مذهبه في كتاب يحمل الناس عليه؛ فقال مالك: أصحاب رسول الله يك تفرقوا في البلاد. وأخذ أهل كل ناحية عمن وصل إليهم؛ فدع الناس وما هم عليه. وكان سيدي ابن سراج رحمه الله يرشح هذاء ويقول: إذا ظهر للمرء خلاف ما يظهر لغيره فيمتنع في ذاته؛ ولا يحمل الناس على مذهبهء فإنه يدخل عليهم شغْبا في أنفسهم وحيرة في دينهم.

ثم بعد ذلك اطلعت على أصول الفتيا للإمام تقي الدين بن الصلاح” قال: إذا ا) سقيان بن سعيد الإمام أبو عبد لله التوري أحد الأعلام علما وزهنا من حبيب بن أبي ثبت وسلمة بن كهيل وابن المتكدر وعنه عبد الرحمن والقطان والفريابي وعلي بن الجعد قال لبن الميارك ما كتبث عن أفضل مته وقال ورفاء لم بر سفيان مثل تفسه توفي في شعبان 161 عن أربع وستين سنة.
anchors:
- Root: ر-خ-ص (rukhaṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Ease, leniency, permission to deviate from the primary ruling due to exigency.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Legal concession (rukhṣah) as a divinely granted facility, contrasted with ʿazīmah (strict resolve).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in juristic usage; metaphorical when applied to moral laxity.
- Root: ن-ه-ي (nahy)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Prohibition, forbidding, restraint.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, the command to abstain entails a command to its opposite, per the Ashʿarī doctrine of the single command’s implicature.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in legal command; metaphorical in ethical counsel (adab).
- Sībawayh Rule: Taḍmīn (Implicit Embedding) — The verb "amara" (to command) may embed the sense of "daʿā" (to summon) when governing a clause of opposition, as in "amara bi-ḍiddihi."
translation:
I say: Al-Shāṭibī said in his "Muwāfaqāt": I have observed that abandoning legal concessions (rukhaṣ) in their proper loci leads to a corruption or corruptions whose weight is grave in the Law. Thus, the one who forbids such a concession has thereby commanded that very corruption; for the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah is that the prohibition of a single thing is a command to its opposite, or to one of its opposites, if it has multiple opposites. Some of them said: They aimed their aspirations at the lofty stations, yet could not attain them. Abū Ḥāmid said: So they abandoned discernment—and that is the very essence of error. Then he transmitted from this meaning, saying: If there are no camels, then sheep will do.

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: Fewness of blame relative to its abundance is a great good. And he said in the "Iḥyāʾ": Thus should you understand the praise of what is praised and the blame of what is blamed; otherwise you would be ignorant of the saying of the speaker: "The pious one's path is the broadest." And the saying: "The good deeds of the righteous are the sins of those brought near (al-muqarrabūn)." And he said in another place: "The permissible acts of the common folk are the sins of the righteous." End quote. And there will come from Ibn Rushd and Ibn al-ʿArabī that the strength of disagreement strengthens the observance of its due regard.

And there will come in the sixth station that what is disputed concerning its lawfulness—its performance is preferable; and that with the Prophet's death, safety is secured from annexing to the obligatory duties what is not of them; and that supererogatory acts (nawāfil), when the Law bears witness to the consideration of their kind, are recommended (mandūbah). Al-Shāṭibī added: And they are taken from the one who sees them in sleep. And there will come at the end of the sixth station that the voluntary acts are those for which the Law determined a reward in their performance, without commanding them, or encouraging them, or performing them. And there will come that assisting in what involves no sin is recommended—perhaps you may be aided by what you forsook of the more excellent for the sake of assistance, with the reward of the beneficent. And Allah the Exalted says: {لَيْسَ عَلَى الضُّعَفَاءِ وَلَا عَلَى الْمَرْضَى} [al-Tawbah: 91].

And there will also come at the end of the sixth station that the prohibition concerning what is within your possession is a prohibition of etiquette (adab) and guidance (irshād). And the prohibition may be of the excellent for the sake of the more excellent; as it is said: It is disliked for one sitting in the mosque to abandon recitation and remembrance; and for the neighbor of Mecca not to perform the pilgrimage every year; and for the married man to practice coitus interruptus. Upon this, Ibn Rushd interpreted the dislike of bequeathing to a dhimmī. And ʿIyāḍ said: What the scholars have disagreed upon concerning its licitness and prohibition—one does not say of it: "forbidden." And he said at the beginning of the "Ikmāl": It behooves not the commander of good and the forbidders of evil to impose upon the people his own ijtihād and his school; rather, he commands only what is agreed upon as good and forbids only what is agreed upon as evil. And Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Nawawī endorsed ʿIyāḍ's words, saying: As for what is disputed, there is no denial therein; and neither the muftī nor the judge may object to one who opposes him, so long as he does not contravene the text of the Qurʾān, the Sunnah, and the consensus. And look at the end of the sixth station of al-Shāṭibī's fatwā: If the people's practice follows a view that is preponderant in consideration, do not oppose them; and let them proceed, for they have emulated it in the earlier age, and practice has run upon it.

And from Ibn Rushd's "Muqaddimāt": What the scholars have disagreed upon concerning its licitness and prohibition—it is disliked (makrūh); and whoever abandons it has a reward; and whoever does it does not sin. And al-Qarāfī and ʿIzz al-Dīn said: Whoever commits a disputed act while believing it forbidden—he is censured for violating the sanctity; but if he believes it licit, he is not censured—unless the basis of the one permitting it is weak, such that the ruling would be overturned by its like in the Law. And Abū ʿUmar said: Do you not see that the Companions disagreed, and they are the exemplars—yet none of them reproached his fellow for his ijtihād, nor harbored resentment against him in himself? To Allah is the complaint; and He is the Succor against a community in whose midst we dwell—a path broad for the one who clings to earnestness in religion, lest honor be deemed licit when opposed. And Abū ʿUmar transmitted with his chain to al-Thawrī, who said: If you see a man acting upon a deed in which there is disagreement, while you hold another view, do not forbid him.

And al-Mahdī commanded that Mālik compile his school into a book to impose upon the people; so Mālik said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispersed across the lands, and the people of each region took from those who reached them; so leave the people and what they are upon. And my master Ibn Sirāj—may Allah have mercy on him—used to endorse this, saying: If a view appears to one person contrary to what appears to another, he refrains in himself, and does not impose his school upon the people; for he would bring upon them turmoil in their souls and confusion in their religion.

Then after that, I came upon the "Uṣūl al-Futyā" of Imam Taqī al-Dīn Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ, who said: If... [text breaks] — Sufyān ibn Saʿīd, the Imām, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Thawrī, one of the leading scholars in knowledge and asceticism, from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, Salamah ibn Kuhayl, and Ibn al-Munkadir; and from him: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, al-Qaṭṭān, al-Firyābī, and ʿAlī ibn al-Jaʿd. Ibn al-Mubārak said: I have not written from anyone more excellent than him. And he said: I have not seen anyone like Sufyān. He died in Shaʿbān 161 AH, at sixty-four years of age.

- Root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Guidance, showing the way; al-Mahdi as "the rightly guided one" — one whom God directs to truth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, hidāyah denotes divine guidance toward salvation, distinct from mere irshād (direction).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical direction; metaphorical: spiritual and moral guidance, as in the caliphal title.
- Root: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Youthfulness, then legal opinion (fatwā) — the act of clarifying an ambiguous ruling.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Iftā' is the authoritative elucidation of divine commands for the community.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: answering a question; metaphorical: issuing a binding religious verdict.
- Root: ق-ض-ي (q-d-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Decree, judgment, fulfilling a matter; qāḍī as one who settles disputes.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qaḍā' in Kalām denotes divine decree; in jurisprudence, judicial determination.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: cutting/deciding; metaphorical: final adjudication.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Clarification) — when a proper noun is followed by a descriptive epithet (e.g., "al-Mahdī: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh"), the second term clarifies the first without a conjunction, maintaining syntactic identity.
translation:
(2) Al-Mahdī: (127–169 AH / 744–785 CE) Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Manṣūr ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAbbāsī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Mahdī bi'llāh: among the caliphs of the ʿAbbāsid state in Iraq. He was born in Bādhāyā (one of the districts of al-Ahwāz), and he assumed rule after the death of his father, by his father's testamentary designation (in the year 158 AH). He remained in the caliphate for ten years and some months, and he died in Māsabadhān, thrown from his mount while hunting. It is also said he was poisoned. He was praiseworthy in his covenant and conduct, kind to his subjects, excellent in character and disposition, generous — it is said that he rewarded a poet with fifty thousand dīnārs. He would sit to hear grievances (maẓālim) and say: "Bring the judges before me, for if my hearing of grievances accomplished nothing but reviving them, that would suffice." He was the first before whom unsheathed swords, axes, arrows, and lances were carried, and the first to play with polo sticks (ṣawālij) in Islam. He it was who built the mosque of al-Ruṣāfah; his tomb is there, and the trace of the mosque has been effaced, and the tomb likewise thereafter.

Then: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (557–643 AH / 1161–1245 CE), ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū ʿAmr, Taqī al-Dīn, known as Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ. A scholar in ḥadīth, jurisprudence, exegesis, and the science of narrators (asmā' al-rijāl). He was born in Shakhān, a town near Shahrazūr. Then he moved to Mosul. He studied jurisprudence under his father ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUthmān Ṣalāḥ al-Dīn, and heard (ḥadīth) from Abū al-Muẓaffar ibn al-Samʿānī, ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn al-Ḥarastānī, al-Shaykh Muwaffaq al-Dīn al-Maqdisī, Ibn ʿAsākir, and others. He traveled to Baghdad, Hamadhān, Nishapur, Marw, Damascus, Aleppo, Ḥarrān, and Jerusalem. Then he returned to Damascus and settled there, and al-Malik al-Ashraf appointed him to teach in the Dār al-Ḥadīth al-Ashrafiyyah. He has numerous works, including: Maʿrifat Anwāʿ ʿUlūm al-Ḥadīth, known as Muqaddimat Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ; al-Amālī; al-Fatāwā; Sharḥ al-Wasīṭ; Fawāʾid al-Riḥlah; Adab al-Muftī wa al-Mustaftī; Ṭabaqāt al-Fuqahāʾ al-Shāfiʿiyyah; and Ṣilat al-Nāsik fī Ṣifat al-Manāsik.

The methodology of the muftī — the ninth section: earnestness in religion. The muftī had a chosen position (mukhtār) which he would adopt for his own self, while informing the one seeking a fatwā of it; he would say to him: "Your school (madhhab) is such-and-such, but what appears to me is such-and-such." And similar to this is what ʿIyāḍ mentioned from Ibn al-Aghbash: he said: He was a consultant in legal rulings, and when he was asked for a fatwā, he would sometimes say: "As for the school of our land, it is such-and-such; but as for what I myself hold, it is such-and-such."

And consider in al-Qaḍāyā of al-Lakhmī concerning the muftī: if one of a married couple asks him about an oath of divorce, does he give him a fatwā, or must both spouses be present — and he rules accordingly, based on whether he deems it correct (taṣwīb) or not. And ʿIyāḍ also transmitted that Qāsim ibn Muḥammad was more learned than Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam. Ibn al-Jabbāb asked him, saying: "Why do I see you giving fatwās to the people regarding what you do not yourself believe?" He replied: "If they asked me about my own school, I would inform them." Qāsim ibn Muḥammad said: "May God benefit us through the disagreement of the companions of Muḥammad ﷺ in their deeds; no one acts upon the deed of any one of them except that he sees himself in ample scope, and sees that one better than him has also acted upon it." And it is also transmitted from him: "Whichever of these you adopt, you will find nothing in your soul against it." And ʿIyāḍ and Muḥyī al-Dīn al-Nawawī said: The school of the verifiers (muḥaqqiqīn) is that every mujtahid is correct (muṣīb). And likewise Abū Ḥāmid said this in his deathbed in Damascus.

Footnotes:
(1) Aḥmad ibn Mubashshir ibn Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, known as Ibn al-Aghbash (d. 328 AH).
(2) Al-Lakhmī: the Imām Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Rabʿī, known as al-Lakhmī; he studied jurisprudence under Ibn Maḥrāz and Abū al-Faḍl ibn Bint Khaldūn, and his fatwās circulated widely; he attained the leadership of Ifrīqiya; al-Māzarī and Abū al-Faḍl al-Naḥwī studied under him. He has a large commentary (taʿlīq) approximating the Mudawwanah. Died 478 AH. Biographed in Tartīb al-Madārik 4/797 and Shajarat al-Nūr 1/117.
(3) Qāsim ibn Muḥammad (d. 276 AH / 889 CE): Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn Qāsim ibn Muḥammad Sayyār al-Qurṭubī, al-Bayyānī (Abū Muḥammad): jurist, ḥadīth scholar, exegete, ḥāfiẓ. Born in Cordoba; traveled to Egypt twice; died in Cordoba. Among his works: al-Īḍāḥ fī al-Radd ʿalā al-Mubtadiʿīn; a book on the solitary report (khabar al-wāḥid); and a tafsīr.
(4) Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam (152–268 AH / 882–899 CE): Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam (Abū ʿAbd Allāh): ḥadīth scholar, ḥāfiẓ, jurist on the school of Mālik, from the people of Egypt. Born in mid-Dhū al-Ḥijjah. He studied jurisprudence under al-Shāfiʿī and Ashab; narrated from Ibn Wahb and others; studied jurisprudence under his father and al-Shāfiʿī; al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Khuzaymah, and many others narrated from him. He was taken to Baghdad on the charge of the doctrine of the creation of the Qurʾān, but he did not answer what they demanded; he returned to Egypt.
(5) Ibn al-Jabbāb: Aḥmad ibn Khālid ibn Yazīd, Abū ʿAmr al-Qurṭubī, known as Ibn al-Jabbāb, the Mālikī ḥadīth scholar. Died in the year 322 AH. He has Qiṣaṣ al-Anbiyāʾ, Kitāb al-Īmān, and Kitāb al-Ṣalāh.

456ه - 995 - 1063م) علي بن أحمد بن سعيد ببن حزم الأندلسي؛ الظاهريء شاعر وكاتب وفيلسوف وففيه. ولد في مديدة قرطبة وكان يلقب القرطي إشارة إلى موئده ونشا. اخثلف في نه أبنحدر من أصول فارسية أم من أصل أسباني أم هو عربي صميم النسب؟ة وعلى كل فقد كانت أسرته من تلك الأسر التي صنعت تاريخ الأندلس. غزت حياته في صياه بالدرس والتحصيل؛ فأخد امنطق عن محمد بن الحسن القرطبي» وأغذ الحديث عن يحيى بن مسعود؛ وأخذ الققه الشافعي عن شيوخ قرطبة؛ ونشأ شافمي المذهب ثم انتقل إلى المذهب الظاهري حتى عرف بابن حزم الظاهري, عاتى اين حزم من الفنة التي شبت بقرطية؛ وكتب متمثلا تلك الفثرة في كتابه طوق الحمامة. في الألفة والألاف. شم شرك قرطية واستقر بمدينة ألمرقة؛ وكان مشغولا بهاجس السياسة وإعادة الخلافة للأمويين. ولقي من جراء ذلك عذابا كثيزاا فظل بعاتي النفي والتشريد بعيدًا عن قرطبة» ويحن للعودة إلبها. ولما سقطت الخلاقة الأموية نهاتيا بالأندلس وزالت دولة الأموين» تفرغ ابن حزم للعلم والتليف. فاثرى المكتبة العربية بمؤلقات مفيدة في مخلف فروع المعرفة من أشهرها: الْضل في الملل والأهوا والبخل؛ طوق الحمامة؛ جمهرة أساب منهج الندلي/ الفا اناسع: الأ بالجذ في الدين 0 علمه وصلاحه عز الدين ابن عبد السلام أنه لا يتعين على العامي إذا قلد إماثنا في مسألة أن يقلده في سائر مسائل الخلاف؛ لأن الناس من لدنّ الصحابة إلى أن ظهرت المذاهب يسألون فيما يسنح لهم العلماء المختلفين من غير تكبر من أحد؛ وسواء اتبع الرخص في ذلك أو العزائم؛ لأن من جعل المصيب واحدًا لم يعينه؛ ومن قال: كل مجتهد مصيب فلا إنكار على من قلد في الصواب. وقال القرافي: انعقد الإجماع على أن من أسلم فله أن يقلد من يشاء من العلماء بغير حجره وأجمع الصحابة أن من استفتى أب يكر وعمر وقلدهما فله أن يستفتي أبا هريرة ومعاذ بن جبل وغيرهما من غير تكير. فمن ادعى رفع هنين الإجماعين عليه الدليل؛ وزاد في "شرح التتفيح”: بشرط ألا يجمع بين الأفوال على صفة تخالف الإجماع؛ وبشرط أن يعتقد في من يقلده الفضل. اه وقد تقدم في صدر الكتاب أن عليه في خاصة نفسه الور والخروج من الخلاف.

.وأما بالنسبة إلى الفتياء فكان سيدي ابن سراج رحمه الله يقول: لا نسع الفنيا والحكم إلا بمشهور المذهب؛ وكان يتقل لنا قول المازري"" بلفظه مستحسنًا له العرب. تفع العروس؛ ورسالته في ييان فضل الأندلس وذكر علمائه؛ الإمامة والخلاقة» الأخلاق والسير في مداواة النفوس والمحلى بالآثارء الاحكام في أصول الأحكام. يُعد ابن حزم درة في تاريخ الأندلس السياسي والفكري والأدبي؛ وقد عاش حياة بالمحن والمصائب: قضاها مناضلً بفكره قله أكثر من أريعين عاماء ولكن فقهاء عصصره حنشوا عليه وألبوا ضده الحاكم والعامة؛ إلى أن أحرقت مؤلفائه ومزقت علاتية باشيلية. اتوفي بقوية متطيشم من بلاد الأنالس.
anchors:
- Root: ق-ل-د (q-l-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To adorn with a necklace (qilādah); to hang something around the neck — hence, to bind oneself to a following.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Taqlīd in theological discourse: acceptance of authority without demanding demonstrative proof (dalīl); contrasted with ittibāʿ (informed following).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: placing a collar; metaphorical: committing one's judgment to another's verdict, as a beast is led by its halter.
- Sībawayh Rule: ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional explicative) — the long genealogical chain of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī functions as an explicative appositive, clarifying the antecedent noun, requiring strict grammatical concord.
translation:
I say: This is the methodology of the one whom God has not widened his breast — the pursuit of the difficult (al-ʿazīmah) in religion — as stated by al-Ghazālī in his "al-Mustaṣfā" and Ibn al-ʿArabī in his "Masālik." He (Ibn al-ʿArabī) said: "We have already clarified this in 'al-Maḥṣūl.'" Then he said: "The correct position transmitted from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī — may God have mercy on him — is that every mujtahid is correct (muṣīb)." He said: "And al-Bāqillānī stated that this is the school of Mālik." Then he said: "This is a sufficient summary for one whom God has granted insight and understanding, in clarifying the soundness of the doctrine affirming the correctness of the mujtahidūn; and it is among the definitive matters (al-qaṭʿiyyāt)." Then he said: "When this is established, and it is impossible that the truth (al-ḥaqq) resides in a single one [exclusively], then the ḥadīth [seemingly indicating otherwise] must be interpreted (taʾwīl)."

And I saw a legal opinion (fatwā) of Ibn ʿArafah regarding the saying of Ibn Ḥazm: "They (the scholars) have agreed that the one who follows the licenses (rukhṣ) is a sinner (fāsiq)." This is refuted by what was issued as a fatwā by the Shaykh whose authority is unanimously agreed upon — the Ashʿarī, the sign, the Imām of the theologians: Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Bishr Isḥāq ibn Sālim ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mūsā ibn Bilāl ibn Abī Burdah ibn the Companion of the Messenger of God — peace and blessings be upon him — Abū Mūsā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays ibn Ḥaḍḍār al-Ashʿarī al-Yamānī al-Baṣrī. His birth was in the year 260 AH; and it is said he was born in the year 270. [Biographical note on al-Ashʿarī, al-Bāqillānī, and Ibn Ḥazm follows.]

And the Shaykh ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām — may God sanctify his secret — said, in his knowledge and righteousness: It is not obligatory upon the layman (al-ʿāmmī), if he has followed an Imām in one matter, to follow him in all other matters of disagreement (masāʾil al-khilāf); because the people, from the era of the Companions until the emergence of the schools (madhāhib), would ask the differing scholars about whatever arose for them, without any one of them being censured. And it is equal in that regard whether one follows the licenses (rukhṣ) or the resolutions (ʿazāʾim); for whoever holds that the correct [answer] is one, has not specified it [for the layman]; and whoever says "every mujtahid is correct" — then there is no objection against one who follows [any scholar] in what is correct.

And al-Qarāfī said: The consensus (ijmāʿ) has been concluded that whoever embraces Islam may follow whichever scholar he wishes, without restriction. And the Companions agreed that whoever sought a fatwā from Abū Bakr and ʿUmar and followed them, may also seek a fatwā from Abū Hurayrah and Muʿādh ibn Jabal and others, without censure. So whoever claims the abrogation of these two consensuses must produce the proof. And he added in his "Sharḥ al-Tanqīḥ": with the condition that he not combine [different] opinions in a manner that violates consensus; and with the condition that he hold a belief in the excellence (faḍl) of the one he follows. End of quote.

And it has already preceded at the beginning of this book that upon him — regarding his own self — is the obligation of scrupulous piety (al-waraʿ) and exiting from disagreement (khurūj min al-khilāf).

As for the matter of issuing fatwās (al-iftāʾ), my master Ibn Sirāj — may God have mercy on him — used to say: "Legal opinion and judgment are not permitted except according to the well-known position (mashhūr) of the school." And he would transmit to us the saying of al-Māzarī, verbatim, expressing approval of it: "The collar of the bride (Taqfīʿ al-ʿArūs)" — and his epistle on the excellence of al-Andalus and the mention of its scholars. [Biographical note on Ibn Ḥazm follows.]

title_en: On the Authority of al-Māzarī Regarding the Limits of Ijtihād, the Reliance on Custom in Fatwā, and the Obligation of Renewed Judgment When Customary Bases Have Vanished
arabic_text:
المازري: محمد (453 - 536ه - 1061 - 1142م). محمد بن علي بين عمر التميمي المئزري المالكي المعروف بالإمام. ؤلد بمازر؛ وهي مديئة بجزيرة صقلية على ساحل البحر المتوسط» كان ذكئا واسع العلم؛ حتى بلغ مرت الاجتهاد في الفقه المالكي» جمع إلى العلم .بالفقه وأصوله؛ العلم بالطب والأدب والرياضيات والكلام. كان يزع إليه في الطب كما يفزع. إيه في الفقه. له مؤلقات كثيرة منها التلقين: وهو كتاب عظيم عند المالكية؛ شرح البرهان لأبي المعالي الجؤيني الفسثى إيضاح المحصول من برهان الأصول؛ الفقليم يفوائد مسلم» التعليقة على المدوتة؛ الكشف والإباء؛ ورد في هذا الكتاب على إحياء علوم الدين للفزالي» وله إملاء على رسائل إخوان الصفاه نظم الفرائد في علم العقائد. وله مؤلف في الطب. توفي بالمهدية بتونس.

وهو ما نصه: ولست ممن يحمل الناس على غير المعروف من المذهب؛ لكثرة من يدعي العلم؛ ويتجاسر على الفتوى؛ ولو فتح هذا الباب لانسع الخخرق على الراقع وهتك حجاب المذهب؛ وهو مفسدة لا خفاء فيها.

وكان يقول أيضًا: وقد يصل المفتي لمدرك أصل بعض المسائل؛ ويجد مرجسًا في نازلة من غير القضية؛ بحيث يدرك فرقًا بينها وبين نص الإمام في مثلهاء. وكثيرا ما يقرر هذا بالنسبة للمقاتل؛ فيقول: إذا شككنا في المقاتل في غير محل الذبح؛ فاحتطنا بعدم إعمال الذكاة يوشك ألا يوافق أحد على ذلك» فإذا قلنا بإعمال الذكاة فنحن على يقين على قول الغير وعلى ريب من قول إمامنا.

وانظر الشيء يذكر بالشيء, انظر الفرق الحادي والستين والماثة لشهاب الدين». قال: لا يحل للمفتي أن يفتي أحدًا بالطلاق حتى يعلم أنه من بلد ذلك العرف الذي ترتبت الفتيا عليهء فإن كان من بلد آخر أفتاه باعتبار حال بلده» قال: وهذه القاعدة في جميع الأحكام كالنقود والسكوك في المعاملات؛ والمنافع في الإيجارات» والأيمان والوصايا والنذور في الإطلاقات. قال: وقد غفل عن هذا كثير من الفقهاء وجدوا الأئمة الأول سطروا في كتبهم فتاوى بناء على عوائدهم؛ فأفتى هؤلاء المتأخرون بهاء وقد زالت تلك العوائدء فكانوا مخطنين خارقين الاجماع؛ فإن الفنيا بالحكم المبني على مدرك بعد زوال مدركه خلاف الإجماع.

ومن ذلك لفظ الحرام والخلية والبرية ونحوهما مما هو مسطور لمالك أنه يلزمه به الطلاق الثلاث بناء على عادة كانت في زمانه. وأكثر المالكية اليوم يفتي بلزوم الطلاق الثلاث بناء على المنقول في الكتب عن مالك وتلك العوائد قد زالت» فلا نجد أحدًا البوم يطل امرأته بالخلية والبرية. وله أيضًا في الفرق التاسع والستين والمائتين: يباح من إكرام الناس قسمان: الأول: ما وردت به الشريعة» كإفشاء السلام.

.والثاني: ما لم يرد في النصوص ولا كان في السلف؛ لأنه لم يكين أسباب اعتباره بلزومه موجودة حيثذ وتجددت في عصرناء فتعين فعله لتجدد أسبابه» كانواع المخاطبات للملوك وأولي الرفعة من العظماء والقيام للإكرام.
anchors:
- Root: م-ز-ر (m-z-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A place of refuge or stronghold; al-Māzarī is the nisba to Māzar, a coastal city in Sicily.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Not a Quranic term; here it designates a proper noun, thus outside theological lexical extension.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally as a toponymic attribution; no metaphorical valence.
- Root: خ-ر-ق (kh-r-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To tear, rend, pierce; a breach in a fabric or barrier.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Metaphorically, the violation of a sacred boundary or legal principle; tearing the veil of the school (madhhab) implies transgression of its protective authority.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: tearing cloth. Metaphorical (majāz): "to widen the tear upon the patcher" — a proverb meaning to aggravate a harm beyond remedy.
- Root: ر-ف-ع (r-f-ʿ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To raise, elevate; also to remove or lift a covering.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Elevation in rank or honor; in legal context, the lifting of a prohibition or the raising of a person's standing.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: to lift physically. Metaphorical: to honor, to elevate in dignity — as in standing up for veneration (al-qiyām lil-ikrām).
- Root: ع-و-د (ʿ-w-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To return, revert; a custom (ʿādah) is that which recurs habitually.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Custom as a secondary source of legal consideration (iʿtibār) when not contradicting revelation; its validity is contingent upon its continued existence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: returning to a place. Metaphorical: habitual practice that shapes legal expectation.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text employs "إذا" (idhā) for conditional temporal clauses and "فإن" (fa-in) for apodosis, requiring precise parsing to distinguish the protasis (condition) from the apodosis (result), especially in the legal hypotheticals regarding doubt in slaughter and divorce.
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

Know that the Imām, the erudite scholar Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿUmar al-Tamīmī al-Māzarī al-Mālikī, known as the Imām — may God have mercy upon him — was born in Māzar, a city on the island of Sicily upon the shore of the Middle Sea. He was possessed of penetrating intelligence and vast learning, such that he attained the rank of absolute ijtihād (martabat al-ijtihād) within Mālikī jurisprudence. He combined, with his knowledge of fiqh and its uṣūl, mastery of medicine, letters, mathematics, and kalām. Men would flee to him in matters of medicine just as they fled to him in matters of fiqh. Among his many compositions are: al-Talqīn, a work of great stature among the Mālikiyyah; his commentary upon al-Burhān of Abū al-Maʿālī al-Juwaynī; Īḍāḥ al-Maḥṣūl min Burhān al-Uṣūl; al-Muʿlim fī Fawāʾid Muslim; his Taʿlīqah upon al-Mudawwanah; al-Kashf wa al-Ibāʾ, in which he refuted the Iḥyāʾ ʿUlūm al-Dīn of al-Ghazālī; his dictations upon the Rasāʾil Ikhwān al-Ṣafā; Naẓm al-Farāʾid fī ʿIlm al-ʿAqāʾid; and a work on medicine. He died at al-Mahdiyyah in Tunisia.

And here is the very text of his words — he said:

"I am not one to burden people with what is not the recognized (maʿrūf) position of the school, because of the multitude of those who claim knowledge and presume to issue fatwā. Were this door to be opened, the tear would widen beyond the patcher's reach, and the veil of the school would be rent asunder — and this is a corruption (mafsadah) whose gravity is not hidden."

And he also used to say:

"The muftī may attain to the very ground (mudrak) of the principle of certain cases, and yet find a scruple (marjis) in a particular incident that falls outside the general ruling — such that he perceives a distinction between that incident and the explicit text (naṣṣ) of the Imām concerning its like. And he frequently affirmed this with respect to the slaughtered animal (muqātil), saying: 'If we entertain doubt concerning the animal at a spot other than the place of slaughter, and we then exercise precaution by declining to apply the ritual slaughter (tadhkiyah), it is unlikely that anyone would agree with us on that. But if we say that the tadhkiyah is to be applied, then we are certain upon the word of another, and in doubt concerning the word of our own Imām.'"

And note the thing by its like — consider the one hundred and sixty-first distinction (al-farq al-ḥādī wa al-sittīn wa al-miʾah) of Shihāb al-Dīn. He said:

"It is not lawful for the muftī to issue a fatwā to anyone concerning divorce (ṭalāq) until he knows that the questioner is from the land of that custom (ʿurf) upon which the fatwā was predicated. For if he is from another land, he should issue the fatwā according to the circumstances of his own land." He said: "And this principle applies to all rulings — such as currencies and coinage in transactions, and usufructs in leases, and oaths, bequests, and vows in their unrestricted formulations." He said: "And many jurists have been heedless of this. They found that the early Imāms had recorded in their books fatwās based upon their own customs; so these later jurists issued fatwās accordingly, even after those customs had vanished — and thus they were mistaken, breaching the consensus (ijmāʿ). For issuing a fatwā on a ruling built upon a ground (mudrak) after that ground has ceased to exist is contrary to consensus."

And of this kind is the expression "al-ḥarām," "al-khaliyyah," "al-bariyyah," and the like — matters recorded of Mālik that the triple divorce (al-ṭalāq al-thalāth) is thereby incurred, based upon a custom that prevailed in his era. Yet most Mālikīs today issue fatwās affirming the incidence of the triple divorce based upon what is transmitted in the books from Mālik, while those customs have long since vanished — for we find no one today who divorces his wife by saying "al-khaliyyah" or "al-bariyyah."

And he also stated, in the two hundred and sixty-ninth distinction (al-farq al-tāsiʿ wa al-sittīn wa al-miʾatayn):

"Two categories of honoring people (ikrām al-nās) are permissible. The first: that which the Sacred Law has prescribed, such as spreading the greeting of peace (ifshāʾ al-salām). The second: that which is found neither in the revealed texts nor in the practice of the Salaf — because the causes warranting its obligatory character did not exist in their time, whereas they have newly arisen in our own age. Thus its performance becomes incumbent, due to the renewal of its causes — such as addressing kings and those of high rank among the great, and standing up for the purpose of honoring them."

title_ar: فهذا كله ونحوه من الأمور العادية: لم تكن في السلف؛ ونحن اليو
title_en: On Novel Customs (Umdūr) and the Station of Religious Zeal (Jidd fī al-Dīn)
arabic_text:
فهذا كله ونحوه من الأمور العادية: لم تكن في السلف؛ ونحن اليوم نفعلهاء منهج اللي الام النابع: الأغلبالجمة في الدين 2 وذلك جائز مأمور به وإن كان بدعة. ولد حضرت عند عز الدين بن عبد السلام: وكان من أعيان العلماء؛ وأولي الجد في الدين والثبات على الكتاب والسنة؛ غير مكترث بالملوك فضلًا عن غيرهم؛ لا تأخذه في الله لومة لائم؛ فقدم له سؤال في القيام الذي أحدثه أهل زمانناء مع أنه لم يكن في السلف؛ هل يحرم؟ فقال: قال رسول الله يق: "لا تباغضواء ولا تقاطعواء ولا تدابروا”: وتترك القيام في هذا الوقت يفضي للمقاطعة والمدابرة» فلو قيل بوجوبه ما كان بعيًا. هذا نص ما كتبه وهو معنى قول عمر بن عبد العزيز'”: تحدث للناس أقضية... الأثر. وهذا بشرط ألا تستبيح محرماء ولا تدرك واجبا. فلو كان الملك لا يرضى منا إلا بمعصية لم يحل لنا أن نواده بذلك. وإنما هذه أمورء لولا هذه الأسباب المتجددة كانت مكروهة من غير تحريمء فلما نجددت هله الأسباب صار تركها يوجب المقاطعة المحرمة: وإذا تعارض المكروه والمحرم حسم مادة المحرم وإن وقع المكروه. وينقسم القيام إلى أقسام الشريعة الخمس. اه ولنرجع إلى ما كنت خرجت منه؛ من أن الأخخذ بالجد في الدين الذي يكون بحيث لو فجأ المرء الموت لم يجد مستزاد. هو الحق الذي لا شك فيه؛ وهو مذهب العارفين» الذين هم أفضل من العلماء بأحكام الله؛ لكن معلوم أن هذا ليس في طوق البشرء فدون هذا المقام مقام آخر؛ هو المقام الثامن.
