(2) عمر بن عبد العزيز (61 - 101 ه - 781 - 720 م) عمر بن عبد العزيز بن مروات بن الحككم الأسوي القرشي؛ أبو حفص: الخليفة الصائح؛ والملك المادل: وريما قبل أله خنامس الخلفاء الراشدين نشييهًا له بهم. وهو من ملوك الدولة المروانية الأموية بالشام. ولد ونشاً. بالمدينة. وولي إمارتها للوليد. ثم استوزره سليمان بن عبد الملك بالشام. ولي الخلافة. بعهد من سليمان سنة 99ه فبوبع في مسجد دمشق. وسكن الناس في أيامه؛ قمنع سب علي ين أبي طالب «وكان من تقدمه من الاموين يسبونه على المتار) ولم تطل مدته؛ قيل: دس له السم وهو بدير سمعان من أرض المعرة: فتوفي به.
anchors:
- Root: ع-م-د (ʿ-m-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of "intending, purposefully undertaking" — an act done with deliberate resolve, not casually.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, ʿamd denotes intentional agency as opposed to accidental occurrence; here it frames the "novel customs" as deliberate communal practices.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) sense is "pillar/prop" (ʿimād); metaphorical (majāz) extension to "customary practice" that upholds social-religious order.
- Root: ج-د-د (j-d-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Newness, renewal" — opposite of oldness; also "earnestness, exertion" (jidd).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, jidd relates to the seriousness of religious commitment, distinct from mere formal compliance.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Majāz: "renewed circumstances" (tajaddud al-asbāb) as a legal cause (ʿillah) altering rulings.
- Root: ق-و-م (q-w-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: "Standing upright" — physical posture of respect or prayer.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Qiyām as a social gesture of honor, distinct from ritual standing in ṣalāh.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Ḥaqīqah: bodily rising; majāz: symbolic deference, which may become obligatory when its omission entails harm.
- Sībawayh Rule: Taʿlīq al-ḥukm bi-al-ʿillah (Conditioning a ruling on its effective cause) — the conditional clause "فلو قيل بوجوبه ما كان بعيدًا" (were it said obligatory, it would not be far) shows hypothetical apodosis governed by the protasis, a standard ʿArabiyyah construction for legal reasoning.
translation:
I say: All this and its like, from among the customary matters, did not exist among the Salaf (the pious predecessors); yet we today practice them. This is the methodology of the Imām, the ocean of knowledge, the preponderant one in religion. And that is permissible, nay commanded, even if it be an innovation (bidʿah).

Indeed, I was present before ʿIzz al-Dīn ibn ʿAbd al-Salām — and he was among the most eminent of scholars, and among those possessed of utmost zeal in religion and steadfastness upon the Book and the Sunnah, heedless of kings, let alone others; no blamer's reproach could sway him in God's cause. A question was presented to him concerning the standing (qiyām) which the people of our time had newly introduced, despite its absence among the Salaf: is it forbidden? He replied: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: {«لَا تَبَاغَضُوا وَلَا تَقَاطَعُوا وَلَا تَدَابَرُوا»} ("Do not hate one another, nor sever ties, nor turn your backs on one another"). And abandoning the standing at this time leads to severance and mutual turning away. So were one to declare it obligatory, that would not be far-fetched. This is the very text he wrote — and it is the meaning of the saying of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz: "New judgments arise for people..." — the well-known athar (report).

And this is conditional upon one not thereby permitting a forbidden thing, nor neglecting an obligatory duty. For if the king would not be pleased with us except through disobedience, it would not be lawful for us to ingratiate ourselves with him by that means. Rather, these are matters which, were it not for these renewed circumstances, would be disliked (makrūh) without being forbidden. But when these causes were renewed, their abandonment came to necessitate the forbidden severance. And when the disliked and the forbidden conflict, the substance of the forbidden is cut off, even if the disliked occurs. And the standing divides into the five categories of the Sacred Law. End of his words.

Let us return to that from which I had departed — namely, that the adoption of zeal in religion, which is such that were death to come upon a person suddenly, he would find no further increase to seek — that is the truth about which there is no doubt, and it is the way of the knowers of God (al-ʿārifūn), who are superior to the jurists concerning God's rulings. But it is known that this is not within the capacity of mortal man. Below this station there is another station — and it is the eighth station.

title_en: The Eighth Station — The Station of the Elite Scholars of Allah’s Ordinances
arabic_text:
المقام الثامن مقام خواص العلماء بأحكام الله تعالى أقول: إنه مقام خواص العلماء بأحكام الله أذ يكون المرء ساعة وساعة: ساعة في مهم؛ وساعة في أهم؛ يشهد لهذا حديث حنظلة"' آخر دونه؛ وهو المقام السابع.

والثاز على انك أني رجت َلفيث أنا ونا تملك دغ خنطا رَضِيٍ الل غل ذْكره لذي صلى اله عليه وسلم. لو قلع تنما تكولون ني لضافختكم الغلابكة يهم الشلام على لوبكم؛ أو انتخو هُذَاء يا حَلظَلَهُ شاغة ؤشاغة. والضيا (63/7: رقم 6469 فك افك قل اربع ره للا :يا ختطلك

المقام السايع أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن في أهم وهو: من لم يقدر أن يكون على عمل أهم؛ فليكن على عمل مهم؛ وقد يضاهي صاحب هذا المقام مقام العارفين بحسن النية؛ وهذا كما قاله مالك وأحمد ابن حنبل”” والشافعي”) وسفيان والزهري” وغيرهم! فقد قال مالك لابن وهب الما جمع كتبه وقام يتقل: ما الذي قمت إليه بأفضل مما كنت فيه؛ إذا أحسنت الني. انقله لبن يونس 0 ونقل أيضًا عن أحمد بسن حنبل: أن رجلا قال له: هذا العلم؛ فمتى العمل؟

ا هو أحمد بن مد بن ثبل بن هلال بن أسد الشياني المروزي َم البندادي؛ أبو غيد اله أحد الأعلام؛ صاحب المذعبء لّة: "المسند" و"الزهد” و"العلل” وغيرهاء ولد سنة 164 وتوف سنة 241 انظر: حلية اأولاء 161/9 و162: وطبقات الحتابلة 10/1 والعير /435.

(2) هو مد بن إدريس بن العباس بن عثمان بن شافع بن السائب القرشي المطلبي؛ فقيه العصرء صاحب المذهب. لّة: "الآم” و'اختلاف الْحَدِيّث" وغيرهماء ولد بغزة سنة 150ه غلّى الأصح؛ وتوفي بمصر سئة 04 انظر: مرآة الجنان 11/2 و12 ووفيات الأعيان 163/4 و165.

(3) هو أبو بكر محمد بن مسلم بن عبيد الدبن شهاب الزهري القرشي المدني؛ ولد سنة اكه أحد أعلام التابعين الإمام العالم العامة الحجة القة النبت؛ روى عن أنس بن مالك وعروة بن الزبر والسائب بن يزيده وروى عنه عطاء بن أبي رباح ومالك بن أنس وعسر بين عبد العزيز. توق سنة 123 (4) غبد الدبن وهب بن مشلم القرشي؛ القهري أبو متمد المصريء الإمام الححافظ ولد سن 125 ومات سنة 196ه أو 197ه له مصنفات كثيرة ما 'الجامع” و"المغازي*. انظر: طبقات خليفة: 297, وتهذيب الكمال 317/4, وسبر أعلام البلاء 223/9.

(5) محمد بن عبد لله بن يونس التميمي؛ الصقلي بو بكر) فقيه؛ فرضي؛ توفي في عشر يفي من ريع الأول. من آثار: كتاب في القرالض: وكتاب جامع للمدونة. انظر؛ العبر: 126/2 طيقات الحفاظ: 309: شذرات الذهب: 242/2.

76 ففال أحمد: ألسنا نحن في عمل؟ وقال الشافمي: طلب العلم أفضل من النافلة. وقال سفيان: ما أعلم عملا أفضل من طلب العلم.

ونقل عياض عن ابن أخي إبن وهب قال: كنت مع عمي بالإسكندرية مرابطاء فاجتمع عليه الناس يسألونه نشر العلم؛ فقال لي: هذا بلد عبادة: وقلما أمهد لنفسي فيه مع شغل الناس؛ فترك الجلوس لهم في الأوقات الني كان يجلس؛ وأقبل على العبادة والحراسة؛ فبعد يومين أناه إنسان» فأخبره أنه رأى نفسه في مشهد عظيم نحو المسجد الحرام والنبي يك فيه وأبو بكر عن يمينه وعمر عن شماله وأنت بين يديهه وفي المسجد قناديل تزهر أحسن شيء وأشدها بياضًاء إذ خفت منها قنديل؛ فاتطفاء فقال لك رسو الله :يا عبد اله أوقده: فأوقدته. ثم آخر كذلك؛ ثم أقمنا ملا فرأيت القناديل كلها همت تطفأء فقال أبو بكر: يا رسول اللهء أما ترى هذه القناديل؟ فقال رسول الله يككِ: هذا عمل عبد الله بن وهب؛ يريد يطفئهاء فبكى ابن وهب: فقال اله ال لأبشرك ولو علمت أنه يغمك لم آنك: فقال له: هو خير؛ رؤياك هذه وعظت بهاء ظنت أن العبادة أفضل من نشر العلم. ثم ترك كثيًا من عمله» ورجع إلى الناس؛ وحبس نفسه عليهم يقرؤون عليه ويسألونه.

وقال الزهري: العالم إذا لم يخل بواجب ولم يقصر في فرض أفضل من العايد.

وستل عز الدين: أقراءة القرآن أفضل أم النظر في العلم؟ فقال: معرفة الأحككام الشرعية أفضل؛ لعموم الحاجة إليها في الفشاوى والأقضية والولايات العامة والخاصة؛ ومصلحة القرآن مقصورة على القارئ؛ وما عمت مصلحته ومست الضرورة والحاجة إليه أفضل مما كانت مصلحته مقصورة على فاعله.
anchors:
- Root: خ-ص-ص (kha-ṣād-ṣād)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning of exclusivity, particularity, and distinction from the general mass (al-ʿāmmah).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Denotes the elect (al-khāṣṣah) whose knowledge penetrates to the divine commands (aḥkām) as opposed to mere outward transmission.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Used literally for selection and setting apart; metaphorically for spiritual rank (maqām) reserved for those singled out by God.
- Root: ه-م-م (hā-mīm-mīm)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Intent, concern, or matter of importance; the heart’s primary occupation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological usage, the hierarchy of concerns (muhimm vs. ahamm) reflects the soul’s orientation toward what is weightier in the scale of divine obligation.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for a burden carried; metaphorical for the weight of religious priority.
- Root: ع-ب-د (ʿayn-bā-dāl)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Service, worship, humble obedience.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The station of the worshiper (al-ʿābid) contrasted with the scholar (al-ʿālim) in the hierarchy of merit.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for ritual devotion; metaphorical for any act of submission to divine command.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Tafḍīl (Preference Construction) — The comparative/superlative pattern (afʿal) governs the ranking of actions, requiring the particle ʿalā or min to mark the object of comparison, as in "afḍal min" (better than).
translation:
I say: This is the station of the elite among the scholars of Allah’s ordinances — that a man be [engaged] hour by hour: an hour in a matter of importance (muhimm), and an hour in a matter of greater importance (ahamm). Witness to this is the ḥadīth of Ḥanẓalah — may Allah be pleased with him — which is [recorded] after this one, and it is the seventh station.

The seventh station is that one be in a matter of importance if not in a matter of greater importance — namely, that he who is unable to be upon a work of greater importance should be upon a work of importance. And the possessor of this station may approximate the station of the knowers (al-ʿārifīn) through good intention (ḥusn al-niyyah). This is as was stated by Mālik, Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, al-Shāfiʿī, Sufyān, al-Zuhrī, and others. For Mālik said to Ibn Wahb — when he had gathered his books and stood to depart: "What you are proceeding to is not better than what you were in, if your intention is good." Ibn Yūnus transmitted this. It is also transmitted from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal that a man said to him: "This is knowledge — when is the [time for] action?" So Aḥmad said: "Are we not in action?" And al-Shāfiʿī said: "Seeking knowledge is better than supererogatory worship (al-nāfilah)." And Sufyān said: "I know of no work better than seeking knowledge."

And ʿIyāḍ transmitted from the nephew of Ibn Wahb, who said: I was with my uncle in Alexandria on coastal guard (murābiṭan), and the people gathered around him asking him to disseminate knowledge. He said to me: "This is a land of worship, and rarely do I find ease for myself in it alongside the occupation of the people." So he abandoned sitting for them in the times in which he used to sit, and turned to worship and guarding. Then after two days, a man came to him and informed him that he had seen himself in a mighty scene toward the Sacred Mosque, with the Prophet — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — in it, Abū Bakr to his right, ʿUmar to his left, and Ibn Wahb before him. In the mosque were lamps (qanādīl) shining with the finest and most radiant light. Then one of the lamps dimmed and was about to go out, and the Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: "O ʿAbd Allāh, kindle it." So he kindled it. Then another [did likewise], and then another, until I saw all the lamps about to go out. Then Abū Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you not see these lamps?" The Messenger of Allah — may Allah bless him and grant him peace — said: "This is the work of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb — they seek to extinguish it." So Ibn Wahb wept, and the man said to him: "I only give you glad tidings; had I known it would grieve you, I would not have come to you." He replied: "It is good — this vision of yours has admonished me, for I had thought that worship was better than disseminating knowledge." Then he abandoned much of his [extra] work, returned to the people, and confined himself to them, as they read to him and questioned him.

And al-Zuhrī said: "The scholar, when he does not neglect an obligation and does not fall short in a duty, is better than the worshiper."

And ʿIzz al-Dīn was asked: "Is reciting the Qurʾān better, or contemplating knowledge?" He said: "Knowledge of the legal rulings (al-aḥkām al-sharʿiyyah) is better, due to the generality of need for it in legal opinions (fatāwā), judgments (aqḍiyah), and public and private authorities (al-wilāyāt al-ʿāmmah wa al-khāṣṣah). The benefit of the Qurʾān is confined to its reciter, whereas that whose benefit is general and to which necessity and need extend is better than that whose benefit is confined to its doer."

title_en: On the Arrangement of Liturgical Wards (Awrād) for Scholars and Students, and the Ruling on Taking Stipends for Religious Offices
arabic_text:
وقال في “الإحياء"؛ لما ذكر أن الطريق إلى الله عمارة الأوقات بالأوراد؛ قال: أما العالم الذي ينتفع الناس بعلمه في فتوى أو تدريس فترتيب أوراده تخالف أوراد العابد؛ فإنه محتاج إلى المطالعة والإقادة؛ فإن أمكنه أن يستغرق أوقاته في ذلك» فهو أفضل ما يشغل به بعد المكتوبات ورواتبهاء قال: وكذلك المتعلم الاشتغال له ِبالتعلم أفضل من النوافل: قال: فحكمه حكم العالم. قد تبين بهذا أن العالم قند يكون من السابقين بنسبة؛ ومن المقتصدين بنسبة؛ ومن الظالمين لأنفسهم بنسية فالذي هو من السابقين فكما قالوا هو الذي لو قيل له: غدًا تموت؛ لم يضع الكتاب من يده؛ والذي من المقتصدين فمن جعل سببه الدنياء فمن قائل يقول: هو خبر من الأسباب» ومن قائل يقول: طلب الدنيا بالدف والمزمار أحب إلي من طلبها بالعلم والدين.

حكى السيد مفتي تونس البرزلي؛ قال: قدم علينا الشيخ الدكالي؛ وكان شيعا صالحًا يأكل من كد يمينه البلغة من القوت» فأنكر أشياء؛ منها: لبس العمامة بغير حتك على ما يليسها اليوم الفقهاء؛ ومنها: أخذ المرتب من الأوقاف على الإمامة وأظن والتدريس؛ حتى أداه ذلك إلى عدم الصلاة خلف الأئمة الذين يصلون بالراتب» فأوجع ذلك سيدنا الإمام؛ فقلت له: نجتمع به؛ ونتكلم معه في هذه المسائل فمنعني. فلما قدر وحججت اجتمعت به في زاوية في الإسكندرية؛ وقلت لله: أنا آخذ المرتب على التدريس والإمامة: وأعتقد أنه أحل إلي من أخذه من بيت المال؛ لأن بيت المال لعموم الناس؛ والمرتب مختص بي من واضعه. وهو إعانة على القول الصحيح لا على معنى الأجرة؛ فلم يكن له جواب: إلا أنه قال: ما قلت ظاهرء إلا أني لا أريد لك هذه السخسخة وفهمت من كلامه أنه كان زاهدًا. اه من نوازله؛ أول النوازل؛ ومن آخرها.

ونقل أيضًا في أولها: اختلف فيما يأخذه الإمام مما حبس عليه بسبب الإمامةء. هل هو كالإجارة أو الإعانة؟ الأول ظاهر كلام الموثقين» والثاتي للبوذري وغيره من اشيوخ شيوخنا. ال وإلى هذا كان يذهب السيد المفتي السرقسطي”'" رحمه الله ونصه: ما يأخذه الإمام على الإمامة من أحباسه؛ أو من أموالهم؛ إجارة على عمله. اه نصه.

وقد تقدم أن من الورع الخروج من الخلاف؛ وسيأتي في المقام السابع: إن لم يقم بالإمامة والعلم حسبة؛ فيكون كمن أخذ إجارة على أن يحج عن غيره: يراعي مقصد المحبس والعاهد. فكما أنه إذا حج عن غيره بعهد عهد له به فتورع عن أن يركع ركعتي الطواف عن غيره؛ فانه يحرم عليه أخذ العهد؛ وكذا إن ترك الزيارة حط (1) هو الشيخ الفقيه الإمام المفتي العالم الحجة البركة المتضنن الصاح المقدس المرحوم أبو عيد لله محمد ين محمد بن محمد الأتصاري السرقسطي رضي اللهعنه.

78 منهج الندلي/ المقام السايع؛ أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن في أمم من العهد قدر ما ينوبها. كذلك ما يأخذه على الوظيف الشرعي براعي قصد العاهد إن فاضلًا ففاضل: وإن مفضولًا فمفضول؛ وإن كان ورع وفعل أفضل منه فبينه وبين وسئل عياض عمن بأكل بدينه؛ فأجاب: هو كأحد الغاصبين: إن كان ظاهرًا كما هو في الباطن؛ وإن كان الذي يظهر أكثر مما يبطن فهو من الآكلين السحت» ونقل السيد مفتي تونس البرزلي هذه القتوى بنصها. اه ولاشك على كل تفصيل: العلم فضيلة: وقراءنه كذلك؛ فيقال: قول تاج الدين في "حكمه": العلم إن قارنته الخشية فلك وإلا فعليك: قأقول: مثل هذا في “الإحياء'. ويقول العلماء في مثل هذا: إنه من تخليط البداية بالنهاية: ومن خلط البداية بالنهاية؛ قطريقه إلى الضلال أقرب منه إلى البداية؛ فاقول قوله: إن قارنته. الخشية فلك» فلا شك أن هذا بالنسبة لمن لم يجعله سيئا؛ وهم السابقون: نفعنا لله بهم.

قال شارح”'' هذه "الحكم": إنه بين فيها طريق العارفين ومنهج السالكين؛ وأما من عدا هؤلاء رضي الله عنهم من مقتصد وظالم لنفسه إذا لم تكن فيه جرحة فالعلم اله رحمة؛ وإن لم تدركه خشية. لا يستوي قط مع من لا علم له؛ وإذا كان المنافق الذي لا يقبل الله منه مثقال ذرة من خير إن قرأ القرآن كالريحانة؛ فكيف بمن يقبل لله منه متقال الذر من الخير إذا قرأ القرآن.

وبالجملة: متقي الشرك إن عمل بما علمء فد أطاع الله طاعتين؛ وإن لم يعلم ولم يعمل؛ فقد عصى الله معصيتين» وإن علم ولم يعمل بمقتضى علمه؛ فقد أطاع الله سبحانه طاعة وعصاه معصية؛ قاله شهاب الدين.
anchors:
- Root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cultivate, to inhabit, to give life to (a place or time); ʿimārah implies active, sustained filling of a space with purposeful habitation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In the spiritual path, ʿimārat al-awqāt signifies the deliberate consecration of time as a sacred precinct (ḥaram) through continuous devotional practice.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: building and populating land. Metaphorical (majāz): investing one's hours with acts that yield eternal merit, as time is the capital (raʾs al-māl) of the servant.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Responsive Construction (al-sharṭ wa-l-jawāb) — The particle "law" (if) introduces a hypothetical protasis whose apodosis is governed by the speaker's epistemic stance, here signaling a counterfactual test of spiritual priority.
translation:
I say — and success is from God alone:

Al-Ghazālī said in the Iḥyāʾ: When he mentioned that the path to God is the cultivation of one's hours with litanies (awrād), he said: "As for the scholar whose knowledge benefits people through legal opinion (fatwā) or teaching, the arrangement of his litanies differs from that of the mere devotee; for he is in need of study and of dictating [to students]. If he is able to devote all his hours to that, then it is the most excellent thing with which he can occupy himself, after the obligatory prayers and their supererogatory regular practices (rawātib)." He said: "Likewise, the student — his occupation with learning is more excellent than supererogatory devotions." He said: "Thus his ruling is the ruling of the scholar."

It has become clear by this that the scholar may be among the foremost (al-sābiqūn) in some respect, among the moderate (al-muqtaṣidūn) in some respect, and among those who wrong their own souls (al-ẓālimūn li-anfusihim) in some respect. As for the one who is of the foremost — it is as they said: he is the one who, if it were said to him, "Tomorrow you will die," would not put the book from his hand. As for the one who is of the moderate — he is the one who makes his knowledge a means for worldly ends. Among the people there are those who say: "It is better than other means," and those who say: "Seeking the world with drum and flute is more beloved to me than seeking it through knowledge and religion."

The Sayyid, Muftī of Tunis, al-Burzulī, narrated: He said: "The Shaykh al-Dakkālī came to us; he was a pious elder who ate from the toil of his right hand, barely enough sustenance (bulghah). He disapproved of certain things — among them: wearing the turban without a chin-strap (ḥanak), as the jurists wear it today; and among them: taking a stipend (murattab) from the endowments (awqāf) for the imamate and, I think, for teaching — until this led him to refrain from praying behind the imams who pray for a salary. This pained our master the Imām greatly. I said to him: 'Let us meet with him and discuss these matters with him.' But he forbade me. Then when I was able and performed the Pilgrimage, I met him in a zāwiyah in Alexandria. I said to him: 'I take a stipend for teaching and the imamate, and I hold it to be more lawful for me than taking from the public treasury (bayt al-māl), because the public treasury belongs to all people, whereas the stipend is specifically assigned to me by its endower. It is an aid (iʿānah) according to the sound opinion, not in the sense of a wage (ujrah).' He had no answer except to say: 'What you have said is apparent, but I do not wish for you this laxity (sakhsakhah).' And I understood from his words that he was a renunciant (zāhid)." End of his citation from his Nawāzil, at the beginning of the Nawāzil; and from its end.

He also transmitted at the beginning of it: "There is disagreement concerning what the imam takes from what is endowed upon him on account of the imamate: is it like a wage (ijārah) or like an aid (iʿānah)? The first is the apparent view of the Muwaqqiqūn (the verifying scholars), and the second is the view of al-Burzulī and others among the elders of our elders. And to this view went the Sayyid Muftī al-Saraqusṭī — may God have mercy on him — and his very words are: 'What the imam takes for the imamate from its endowments, or from their properties, is a wage for his work.' End of his words."

It has already preceded that part of scrupulous piety (waraʿ) is to exit from disagreement (al-khurūj min al-khilāf). And it will come in the Seventh Station: If one does not perform the imamate and knowledge as a gratuitous service (ḥisbah), then he is like one who takes a wage to perform the Pilgrimage on behalf of another: he must observe the intention of the endower (al-muḥabbis) and the contractor (al-ʿāhid). For just as it is the case that if one performs the Pilgrimage for another by a contract contracted with him, and he then exercises scrupulous piety by not performing the two rakʿahs of the circumambulation (ṭawāf) on behalf of the other — for it is unlawful for him to take the contract [for that] — likewise, if he abandons the visitation (ziyārah), then he must reduce from the contract amount whatever corresponds to it. Similarly, what he takes for the legitimate office (al-waẓīfah al-sharʿiyyah) must observe the intention of the endower: if it is excellent (fāḍil), then [he takes] as excellent; if it is deficient (mafḍūl), then as deficient; and if he is scrupulously pious and does what is more excellent than it, then between him and God.

And ʿIyāḍ was asked about one who eats by means of his religion. He answered: "He is like one of the two usurpers (al-ghāṣibayn): if his outward appearance is as his inward state, then he is a usurper; and if what appears is more than what he conceals, then he is among those who devour illicit gain (suḥt)." And the Sayyid Muftī of Tunis, al-Burzulī, transmitted this legal opinion (fatwā) verbatim. End.

There is no doubt, upon every detail: knowledge is a virtue, and its recitation is likewise. Thus one may say regarding the saying of Tāj al-Dīn in his Ḥikam: "Knowledge — if fear (khashyah) accompanies it, then it is for you; otherwise, it is against you." I say: Something like this is in the Iḥyāʾ. And the scholars say concerning such a statement: It is of the confusion of the beginning with the end (takhlīṭ al-bidāyah bi-l-nihāyah). And whoever confuses the beginning with the end, his path to misguidance is nearer than to the beginning. So I say regarding his words, "If fear accompanies it, then it is for you" — there is no doubt that this is relative to the one who has not made it an evil; and they are the foremost (al-sābiqūn). May God benefit us by them.

The commentator on these Ḥikam said: "He explained in it the way of the knowers of God (al-ʿārifīn) and the methodology of the wayfarers (al-sālikīn). As for those other than these — may God be pleased with them — from among the moderate and the self-wronging, if there is no defect (jarḥah) in them, then knowledge is for them a mercy, even if fear does not overtake them. It is never equal to the one who has no knowledge. And if the hypocrite — from whom God accepts not even an atom's weight of good — if he recites the Qur'an, he is like the sweet basil (rayḥānah); then how much more [is the case of] the one from whom God accepts an atom's weight of good when he recites the Qur'an?"

In sum: The one who is free of shirk — if he acts upon what he knows, then he has obeyed God with two obediences; and if he does not know and does not act, then he has disobeyed God with two disobediences; and if he knows but does not act upon the requirement of his knowledge, then he has obeyed God — glorified be He — with one obedience and disobeyed Him with one disobedience. This was said by Shihāb al-Dīn.

title_en: The Eighteenth Station: On the Etiquette of Seeking Knowledge and Its Sincerity

فقد حصل من هذا أن العلم نعمة والعمل به نعمة يسألهما العبد من ربه مفرقين فيقول: اللهم أرني الحق حمًا وارزقني اتباعه؛ وأرني الباطل باطلًا وارزقني اجتتايه. اه ثم إذا لم يكن العلم يورئه خشية: فلا يزهد في قراءته؛ لأنه كما تقدم نعمةء لكن ينبغي أن يكون في قراءنه متأدبًا بآداب الشرع؛ وحينشذ تسوغ له الجراية عليه (1) هو محمد بن إيراهيم بن عباد الفزي الرئدي الشاذلي. المتوفى: سنة 792 والأجر. ولا يؤيسه من العلم قول ناج الدين: إن العلم إذا لم تقارنه خشية أنه على قارئه نقمة فقط ما هو كذاء كما تقدم للإمام الموثوق بدينه شهاب الدين. وما يقال هذا إلا في العلوم المذمومة؛ كعلم السحر والطلمسات: وأما العلوم الخادمة اللشريعة؛ فقراءتها حسنة؛ والمرتب على ذلك سائغ إذا كان القارئ فبه أهلية ذلك» وقرأه على ما ينبغي؛ فأول ذلك أن يعتني بما ينبني عليه عمل من الدين؛ ويكون في طلب العلم كمنشد ضالة» كما قاله ي: "الحكمة ضالة المؤمن””» لا يفرق بين أن تظهر الضالة على يده أو على يد من يقرأ معه معيئًا لا خصمّاء ويشكر له إذا عرفه الخطا أو أظهر له الحق» كما لو أخذ طريقًا في طلب ضالته: فينبهه صاحبه على ضالته في موضع آخرء أكان يشكره أم يذمه؟ وأكان يكرهه أم يفرح به؟ وكذا الشيخ مع التلميذ والتلميذ مع الشيخ: كلاهما لا تكون همته إلا في إصلاح متن؛ وتكميل نقص؛ وتبيين ما أشكل؛ هكذا قاله بعضهم؛ وأنا أقول: تييين ما أشكل ليس بمتعين على المقلد. إنما المطلوب إصلاح المتنء وتصوير النص؛ وتكميل النقص.

.وأما تبين ما أشكل ونقل الخلاف؛ فإن قلت أنت: إنه مهم؛ فأقول أنا: ليس بأهم. الأوثى لكل ذي عزم وحزم أن يبدأ في العلم بالأهم فالأهم؛ قال السيد مفتي تونس البرزلي: لا يخلو السائل للعالم من أربعة أوجه: مسترشد واجب على العالم دلالته» علامة ذلك في السائل: قبوله وتسليمه؛ ومستفهم واجب على العالم هدايقه؛ وعلامة ذلك في السائل: بحثه بالرفق» وطلب الدليل بالوقار ومستخبر واجب على الإمام الإعراض عنه؛ والتنزء عن الجدال والخصومة والتعريض بالله وبرسوله ويأئمة الدين؛ للرد عليهم. والتكذيب لهم؛ ومفتون بالدعوى مستدرج بالرؤية لحاله واجب على العالم الصمت عنه.

ونقل الماوردي أن قومًا تحققوا بالعلم تحقق المتكلمين: واشتهروا به اشتهار المنحرفين؛ إذا أخذوا في المناورة ظهر كلامهم؛ وإذا سئلوا عن واضح المذهعب ضلت أفهامهم؛ حتى أنهم يتخبطون في الجواب خبط عشواء؛ فلا يظهر لهم صواب ولا يتقرر منهم جواب: ولا يرون ذلك نقضًا إذا لفقوا على المخالف حججًا مألوفة وهم قد جهلوا من المذهب ما يعلمه المبتدئ.

50 منج الندلي/ المقام اسايع؛ أن يكون في مهم إن لم يكن في أمم وقال أبو الدرداء رضي الله عنه: لا تتعلموا العلم لتتجملوا به؛ فإئه يوشك إن طال بكم عمر أن يتجمل أحدكم بعلمه كما يتجمل ذو البزة ييزته. ونقل ابن أبي زيد” في صدر "مختصره": قال نبينا عليه السلام: “من تعلم العلم ليساهي به أو ليرائي به؛ أرقفه الله موقف الذل؛ وجعله عليه حسرة يوم امة"”2» ولا يقال: هذه الآفة من قراءة العلم إنما هي من خبث الدخيلة كالمنافق يقرأ القرآن» ولذلك قال ربيعة: لا تعلموا العلم سفهاءكم: فيصرقوا أخلاقهم فيه وقال وهب بن منبه: العلم كالغيث ينزل من السماء حلوًا صافيا فتشريه الأشجار فتحوله على قدر طعومهاء يزداد المر مرارة: والحلو حلاوة. فالقائل: أعوذ بالله من العلمء يضاهي من يقول: أعوذ بالله من الغيث. وقال الشاطبي: أجاز النظار أن يتصور الاجتهاد في الشريعة من غير المسلم. وذون بلله من الفاجر العالم بالسنة. وروى ابن ماجه”' بسند جيد: قيل: 8 المنكر؟ فقال تقة: 'إذا ظهر الإدهان في خياركم والفقه في أراذلكم”*. وقال ربيعة: لا تعلموا العلم سفهاءكم؛ فيصرفوا أخلاقهم فيه؛ وقد نقدم قول وهب بن منبه وقال مكحول”: بفقه الرعاع فساد الدنياء ويفقه السفلة فساد الدين.

(1) هو ابن ني زيد لقيرواتي» عبد اله ين عبد الرحمن (المتوفى: 386ههم الواسطى قال الطبراني والبزار تفره به سليمان: زا الطبراني: ولم ينابع عليه وقال صاحب الميزاذ: لا ندري من ذا. والضياء (72/7: رقم 2480).
anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge as the indelible mark or trace (wasm) left upon the heart by the thing known; the faculty of discerning truth from falsehood.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIlm as the apprehension of a thing as it truly is (idrāk al-shayʾ ʿalā mā huwa bihi), encompassing both the act of knowing and the known object; its opposite is jahl (ignorance), not mere nescience.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes certitude (yaqīn) and firm comprehension; metaphorically (majāz), it may refer to the known object itself or to the means of knowing (dalīl).
- Root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Reverential fear that impels flight toward God, distinguished from mere khawf (fear of a thing) by its admixture of awe and veneration.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Khashyah as the fear born of maʿrifah (gnosis) of the Majestic—the fear of the knower, not of the ignorant; it is the fruit of ʿilm and its intended perfection.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: dread of a harmful thing; metaphorical: the awe that restrains the soul from transgression, as in {«إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ»} (Fāṭir: 28).
- Root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Wandering from the path; the lost object (ḍāllah) that its owner seeks with diligence, implying prior possession and subsequent loss.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Ḍalāl as deviation from the straight path (ṣirāṭ mustaqīm), whether in belief, speech, or action; its opposite is rushd (right guidance).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical straying; metaphorical: intellectual or spiritual error, as in the ḥadīth "al-ḥikmah ḍāllat al-muʾmin" where wisdom is likened to a lost camel the believer seizes wherever found.
- Root: ج-د-ل (j-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The twisting and plaiting of ropes; hence, disputation as the intricate weaving of argument, often implying contention.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Jidāl as argumentation that may be praiseworthy (bi-llatī hiya aḥsan) or blameworthy (bi-gḥayr ḥaqq), depending on intent and method.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the firm twisting of cords; metaphorical: the contentious exchange of proofs, where the disputant seeks to "twist" the opponent's position.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of ʿAṭf al-Bayān (Appositional Coordination) — When two nouns are coordinated without a conjunction to clarify or specify the first, as in "اللهم أرني الحق حقًا" where the second "ḥaqqan" is a taʾkīd (emphatic apposition) reinforcing the first, not a new entity.
translation:
I say: It has thus been established that knowledge is a blessing, and acting upon it is a blessing—two blessings which the servant beseeches from his Lord as distinct requests, saying: "O Allah, show me the truth as truth and grant me its following; and show me falsehood as falsehood and grant me its avoidance." End.

Then, if knowledge does not engender in him reverential fear (khashyah), let him not abstain from reading it; for as has preceded, it is a blessing. However, he ought to be, in his reading of it, adorned with the etiquettes of the Sacred Law; and in that case, it is permissible for him to continue upon it and to receive its reward. Nor should the saying of Najm al-Dīn despair him of knowledge—that knowledge, when not accompanied by fear, is but a punishment upon its reader. That is merely a statement of the sort we have already mentioned from the Imām whose religion is trusted, Shihāb al-Dīn. And such a saying is only applied to the blameworthy sciences—like the science of sorcery and talismans. As for the sciences that serve the Sacred Law, their reading is commendable; and the reward consequent upon that is permissible when the reader possesses the requisite competence therein and reads it as it ought to be read.

The foremost of that is that he should attend to what the practice of religion is built upon; and he should be in his pursuit of knowledge like one seeking a lost object (ḍāllah)—as it has been said: "Wisdom is the lost object of the believer." He does not distinguish between the lost object appearing at his own hand or at the hand of one who reads with him as a helper, not an adversary. And he thanks him when he points out his error or shows him the truth—just as if he had taken a path in seeking his lost object, and his companion alerted him to his lost object in another place: would he thank him or blame him? Would he resent him or rejoice in him? Likewise is the relation of the shaykh with the student and the student with the shaykh: neither of them has any concern save the rectification of the text, the completion of deficiency, and the clarification of what is obscure. Thus said some of them. But I say: The clarification of what is obscure is not incumbent upon the blind follower (muqallid). What is required is only the rectification of the text, the accurate rendering of the wording, and the completion of deficiency.

As for clarifying what is obscure and transmitting the points of disagreement—if you say that it is important, I say: it is not the most important. The most fitting for every one possessed of resolve and firmness is to begin in knowledge with the most important, then the next most important. Said the Sayyid, the Muftī of Tunis, al-Burzulī: "The questioner of a scholar is not free from four aspects: (1) A seeker of guidance (mustarshid)—upon the scholar is the obligation to direct him; the sign of this in the questioner is his acceptance and submission. (2) A seeker of understanding (mustafhim)—upon the scholar is the obligation to guide him; the sign of this in the questioner is his gentle inquiry and his request for proof with dignity. (3) A tester (mustakhbir)—upon the Imām is the obligation to turn away from him, and to abstain from argumentation, contention, and the disparagement of Allah, His Messenger, and the Imāms of the religion, in response to them or in denial of them. (4) One deluded by his own claim, lured by the vision of his state—upon the scholar is the obligation of silence regarding him."

And al-Māwardī transmitted that a people attained to knowledge with the attainment of the speculative theologians (mutakallimūn) and became renowned with the renown of the deviants: when they engaged in skirmishing, their speech appeared; but when asked about the clear points of the school (madhhab), their understandings strayed—so much so that they floundered in their answers like one groping in the dark (khabṭ ʿashwāʾ). No correctness appears from them, nor is any answer established from them. Yet they do not consider this a defect, for they have patched together against the opponent familiar arguments, while they are ignorant of the school to a degree that even the beginner knows.

And Abū al-Dardāʾ—may Allah be pleased with him—said: "Do not learn knowledge to adorn yourselves with it; for it is likely that, if your life is prolonged, one of you will adorn himself with his knowledge as the wearer of fine garments adorns himself with his attire." And Ibn Abī Zayd transmitted at the beginning of his Mukhtaṣar: Our Prophet—peace be upon him—said: "Whoever learns knowledge to vie with others (lisāhī) or to show off (liriyāʾ), Allah will stand him in the station of humiliation and make it a cause of regret for him on the Day of Resurrection." And it is not said that this affliction arises from the reading of knowledge itself; rather, it arises from the corruption of the inner self (dakhīlah)—like the hypocrite who recites the Qurʾān. For this reason, Rabīʿah said: "Do not teach knowledge to your foolish ones (sufahāʾukum), lest they corrupt their characters within it." And Wahb ibn Munabbih said: "Knowledge is like the rain that descends from the sky, sweet and pure; the trees drink it and transform it according to their tastes—the bitter increases in bitterness, and the sweet in sweetness." So the one who says, "I seek refuge in Allah from knowledge," resembles the one who says, "I seek refuge in Allah from rain." And al-Shāṭibī said: "The speculative theologians (nuẓẓār) permitted the conception of ijtihād in the Sacred Law from a non-Muslim—and how much more so from a wicked man learned in the Sunnah!" And Ibn Mājah narrated with a good chain: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, when will the reprehensible (al-munkar) appear?" He said: "When flattery (idhān) appears among your virtuous ones and jurisprudence (fiqh) among your base ones (arādhilukum)." And Rabīʿah said: "Do not teach knowledge to your foolish ones, lest they corrupt their characters within it"—and the saying of Wahb ibn Munabbih has already preceded. And Makḥūl said: "The jurisprudence of the rabble (al-ruʿāʿ) is the corruption of the world, and the jurisprudence of the lowly (al-siflah) is the corruption of the religion."

(5) مكحول الشامي (..- 112ه -..- 730 م) هو مكحول بن أبي مسلم شهراب بن شاة .وكان سفيان إذا رأى هؤلاء الفبط يكتبون العلم يتغير وجهه فقيل له في ذلك فقال: كان العلم في سادات الناس؛ فإذا خرج وصار إلى هؤلاء غير الدين؛ وهذا كما قبل: لا يخون أمين؛ ولككن إذا انتمن الخخائن خمان» ونقل عياض في "مداركه". تقديم من أخر الله وتأخير من قدم الله فتئة في الأرض وفساد كبيره وقال ابن مسعود: الا يزال الناس بخير ما أخحذوا العلم من أكابرهم» فإذا أخحذوه عن أشرارهم ضلواء وقال عمر رضي الله عته: قد علمت متى صلاح الناس ومتى قسادهم؛ إذا جاء الفقه من قبل الصغير استعصى عليه الكبير؛ وإذا جاء من قبل الكبير تابعه الصغير .ونقل أبو عمر يسنده أن عطاء الخراسائي”'' كان إذا صلى يتكلم يكلمات» فغاب يوماء فتكلم رجل من المؤذنينء فسمع رجاء بن حيوة”» صوته: فقال: من هذا؟؛ قال: أناء قال: اسكت؛ فإنا نكره أن نسمع الخير إلا من أهله. ناب فيس”" من الخمر في الجاهلية؛ فجمع بنيه عند موته؛ وقال لهم: يا بني؛ احفظوا عني؛ فلا أحد نبو عبد اله الهذلى بالولاء: فقيه الشام في عصره؛ من حفاظ الحديث. أصله من فارس» ومولده يكابل. ترعرع بها وسبى؛ وصار مولى لامرأة بمصرء من هذيل؛ قتسب إليها. وأعتق وتفقه؛ ورحل في طلب الحديث إلى العراق؛ فالمدينة: وطاف كثيرًا من الإلدان. واستقر في دمشق. وتوفي بها. غال الزهري: لم يكن في زمنه أبصر منه بافتيا. وكان في لسائه عجمة: يجمل القاف كاف الا 5 ا) عطاء الخراساتي هو عطاء بن ميسرة وكنية ميسرة أبو مسلم إلا أن مالا روى عنه وقال: عطاء لين عبد اله. وقيل له: الخراساني لأنه تقل الى خراسان وتولى القضاء بهاء من عليه قال الحافظ في التغريب 392/1: صدوق يهم كثيزا وبرسل وبدلس.

وانظر قول الإمام الماوردي: إذا أخذوا في المناظرة ظهر كلامهم؛ وإذا سثلوا عن واضح المذعب ضلت أفهامهم. قال في "الإحياء": أي فائدة في المناظرة لمن ليس له رتبة الاجتهاد؟ وهو حكم كل أهل العصر الذي لو ظهر له ضعف مذهب مقلده لم يجز له أن يتركه؛ بل يجب عليه أن يقول: ولعل لمقلده مدرك لم يدركه. ثم قال: ومن وظائف المتعلم الاحتراز من الإصغاء إلى اختلاف الناس» فإن إصغاء الذلك يدهش عقله؛ ويحير ذهنه؛ ويفتر رأيه؛ ويؤيسه من الإدراك والاطلاع» بل .ينبغي أن يتقن أولا الطريقة الواحدة المرضية عند أستاذهه فإن كان أستاذه من عادته انقل المذاهب» فليحذر منه فإن إضلاله أكبر من إرشاده؛ ولا يصلح الأعمى لقود العميان وإرشادهمء ومن هذه حاله فهو يعد في عمى الحيرة وتيه الجهل.
anchors:
- Root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To exit, to depart from a place or state; also to extract or bring forth.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Used for the emergence of something from its proper locus; here, knowledge (ʿilm) departing from its people of merit (ahluhu) to those unworthy of it.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal in physical exit; metaphorical here for the transmission of sacred knowledge from worthy bearers to base ones, marking a corruption of order.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional Clause with Inna (الشّرط مع إنّ) — The construction «إذا جاء الفقه من قبل الصغير...» uses temporal-conditional idhā governing a nominal sentence, indicating a recurrent, habitual consequence rather than a single event.

(3) He is Abū ʿAbd Allāh Muḥammad ibn Yazīd ibn Mājah al-Qazwīnī. And it is well known that "Mājah" is with the letter hāʾ (هاء) at the point of pause, being assimilated therein — like "Dāsah" and "Mindah." That is to say, one does not say "Mājah" [with tāʾ marbūṭah]; although some have chosen that [pronunciation]! This is because, since the Arabs came to use it [as a proper name], it acquired the status of an Arabic noun. But the original form is with the hāʾ: "Mājah," and likewise "Mindah" and "Dāsah." He died in the year two hundred and seventy-three (273 AH / 886 CE). (4/185): This is a sound chain of transmission (isnād ṣaḥīḥ), whose narrators are trustworthy (thiqāt). It was also transmitted by al-Ḍiyāʾ (7/227, no. 2667), who said: "Its chain is sound." Al-ʿUqaylī mentioned it (2/91, biography 547: al-Zubayr ibn ʿĪsā al-Ḥumaydī) and said: "None has followed him [in this narration], and it is known only through him." Abū Nuʿaym also mentioned it in al-Ḥilyah (5/185) and said: "It is gharīb (singular/strange in transmission)."

(5) Makḥūl al-Shāmī (d. 112 AH / 730 CE) — he is Makḥūl ibn Abī Muslim Shahrab ibn Shāh. He was a client (mawlā) of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hudhayl by allegiance (walāʾ); he was the jurist (faqīh) of Syria in his time, and one of the preservers of ḥadīth (ḥuffāẓ). His origin was from Persia, and his birthplace was Kābul. He grew up there and was taken captive; he became a client of a woman in Egypt, from [the tribe of] Hudhayl, and was attributed to her. He was freed, acquired jurisprudence, and traveled in search of ḥadīth to Iraq, then to Medina; he toured many lands and settled in Damascus, dying there. Al-Zuhrī said: "In his time, there was none more perceptive than him in issuing legal opinions (fatwā)." There was a foreign accent in his speech; he would pronounce the qāf as kāf.

And Sufyān — when he saw these Copts (al-qibṭ) writing down knowledge — his face would change. It was said to him about that, and he replied: "Knowledge was among the nobles of the people (sādāt al-nās); when it departed and came to these, the religion was altered." This is as the saying goes: "The trustworthy one does not betray; but when the treacherous are entrusted, they betray." And ʿIyāḍ transmitted in his Madārik: "Advancing whom Allah has delayed, and delaying whom Allah has advanced, is a tribulation (fitnah) in the earth and a great corruption."

Ibn Masʿūd said: "The people will not cease to be in goodness so long as they take knowledge from their elders (akābirihim). But when they take it from their wicked ones (ashrārihim), they will go astray."

And ʿUmar — may Allah be pleased with him — said: "I have known when the people's rectitude comes and when their corruption comes: when jurisprudence (fiqh) comes from the young one (al-ṣaghīr), the elder (al-kabīr) resists it; and when it comes from the elder, the young one follows him."

Abū ʿUmar transmitted with his chain that ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī — when he prayed, he would speak some words [after it]. One day he was absent, and a man among the muʾadhdhins spoke; Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah heard his voice and said: "Who is this?" He said: "I am [so-and-so]." He said: "Be silent! For we dislike hearing the good (al-khayr) except from its people (ahluhu)."

He (i.e., Makḥūl) drank wine in the Jāhiliyyah; so he gathered his sons at his death and said to them: "O my sons, preserve from me: no one is more sincere to you than I — if I were in a matter, I would not be in any matter more sincere to you than this. So make your elders leaders (sawwidū kibārakum), and do not make your young ones leaders; lest the people treat your elders as foolish, and you become contemptible in the eyes of the people."

(1) ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī is ʿAṭāʾ ibn Maysarah, and the kunyah of Maysarah is Abū Muslim — except that some who narrated from him said: "ʿAṭāʾ, the client of ʿAbd Allāh." He was called al-Khurāsānī because he moved to Khurāsān and undertook the judgeship (qadāʾ) there. Al-Ḥāfiẓ said in al-Taqrīb (1/392): "Truthful (ṣadūq), but he errs much, and he commits irsāl and tadlīs."

(2) Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywah — Jarwal al-Kindī, Abū al-Miqdām: the elder (shaykh) of the people of Syria in his time; one of the eloquent preachers and scholars. He was constant in attendance upon ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz during both his governorship and his caliphate; Sulaymān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik made him his secretary (istaktabahu). It was he who advised Sulaymān to appoint ʿUmar as his successor, and he had notable accounts with him.

(3) Qays ibn ʿĀṣim al-Tamīmī al-Minqarī — he lived to the age of nine [i.e., ninety?] and was a noble, intelligent, forbearing, and generous man. The Prophet ﷺ said of him: "This is the master of the people of the desert (sayyid ahl al-wabar)." He settled in Basrah, and from him narrated al-Aḥnaf, al-Ḥasan, and a group.

Consider this alongside what Ibn al-ʿArabī transmitted in his Sirāj, in the name of the ninety-seventh [station], which is humility (al-tawāḍuʿ).

And consider the saying of Imām al-Māwardī: "When they engage in disputation (munāẓarah), their speech becomes apparent [in its weakness]; and when they are asked about the clear points of the school (wāḍiḥ al-madhhab), their understandings go astray."

He said in al-Iḥyāʾ: "What benefit is there in disputation for one who has not attained the rank of ijtihād?" And this is the ruling for all the people of this age: if the weakness of the school of his taqlīd becomes apparent to him, he is not permitted to abandon it; rather, he must say: "Perhaps my imām has a ground of proof (mudrak) that I have not grasped."

Then he said: "Among the duties of the student is to guard against listening to the disagreements of the people — for listening to that bewilders his intellect, confounds his mind, weakens his judgment, and makes him despair of comprehension and insight. Rather, he should first master the single path (al-ṭarīqah al-wāḥidah) that is pleasing to his teacher. And if his teacher is one whose habit is to shift between schools (naql al-madhāhib), then let him beware of him — for his misguidance is greater than his guidance. The blind man is not fit to lead the blind or to guide them; and whoever is in this state is counted among the blind of confusion and the wandering of ignorance."

title_en: On the Limits of Obligatory Knowledge and the Danger of Partisan Disputation
arabic_text:
.وقال المازري: كنت بين يدي أستاذي في الأصول؛ فجاء الثبت أن اليوم من رمضان؛ فقلت: هذا اليوم لا يقضى على رواية مالك وبعض أصحابه. فأخخذ بأذني أستاذي وقال لي: إن قرأت العلم على هذاء فلا تفرأه؛ فإنه يجيء منك زنيديق بهذه اللفظة تصغير زنديق؛ وقد يكون بعضهم كما قال ابن محرزا'' في مسألة من تداخل العدد قال: من لم يبلغ فكره إلى معرفة المعنى يفزع إلى الاستراحة من أتعاب فكره إلى التعلق بظاهر الاختلاف. اه فانظر من كانت همته في القراءة فأي ثمرة تكون له في الخارج في فتوى أو عبادة. وما العلم إلا للعمل؛ وسيآتي في الكلام على هذا المقام في الترقي: أنه لا ينبغي للمقتصد في قراءة العلم فضا عن السابق في الخيرات أن يتغمر في جدل.

(1) محمد بن محرز (569 - 655 ه- 1174 - 1267 م محمد بن محمد بن أحمد بن عبد الرحمن وعرف باين محوز محدث؛ حافظ. مؤرخ. لغوي. ولد في آخر جمادى؛ وتوفي ببجابة في 18 شوال. له تقييد على التلقين.

قالوا: ولا يلزم المرء معرفة الجوهر والعرض؛ إذ مات الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم ولا عرفوهماء ولا يلزمه أيضًا أن يعرف هل الاسم المسمى أولاء ولا تفسير الأحاديث الشي فيها الوجه واليد والاستواء والككلام والتنزل والرؤية والكرسي والضحك ومسح ظهر آدم؛ وأن (قل هو الله أحد) تعدل ثلث القرآن: ولا يسأل المرء يوم القيامة عن القضاء والقدر ولا يلزمه أن يعلم حكم الأطفال الذين ماتوا صغارًاه ولا فلان أفضل من فلان ولو كان صحايئاء ولا هل مع الكفار ملائكة: ولاه حكم بأجوج ومأجوج؛ ولا هل الروح عرض أو جسم؛ ولا كيفية قبض الروح؛ ومحاجة آدم موسى؛ ورؤية النبي يك لعيسى والدجال؛ ولا معنى: "نقص من أجره آقيراط”؛ ولا معنى: "إنما نسمة المؤمن طائر”"» و”مدى صرت المؤذن””» و"عقد الشيطان على قافية الرأس””/ وكيفية أكل الشياطين؛ وشربهم؛ ولا معتى: "أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف””"؛ ولا: 'يزني الزاني حين يزني وهو مؤمن”" ولا كيفية ميزان الأعمال يوم القيامة. ولا الفرق بين الفقير والمسكين: ولا معنى: "لا ضرر ولا ضرار””؛ و'لا تحسسواء ولا تجسسوا””' ولا معنى: الذاريات؛ والمرسلات»

(3) أعرجه البخاري (383/1: رقم 1091)» ومسلم (776). رقم 8939 وأعرجه أيضا: أحمد (127/5: رقم 21210) والطيالسي (ص 76 رقم 6558. وقال: حسن صحيح غريب. وأخرجه أبضّا: أحمد (479/2: رقم 10220) والبخاري :2097/6 رقم 6425 ولين حبان (260/10: رقم 4412, هذا إسناد فيه جابر (يعني الجعفي) وقد اتهم. والطبراني (228/11: رقم 11576).

ز7) أخرجه البخاري (1976/5؛ رقم 44849 ومسلم (1985/4؛ رقم 2563» وبر دارد 80/4 0 منهج الندلي/ الفامالسايع: ايكون في مهم إن لم يكن في لم والميسرء والآب. ولا متى الساعة: ولا يلزمه أيضًا أن يتعلم من صناعة النحو إلا مؤدي إلى الوقوف على كيفية التكلم. وأن ما عدا ذلك فإنه فضول؛ كرافع المبتدأء وناصب الظرف خيزا.
anchors:
- Root: ث-ب-ت (th-b-t)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Firmness, stability, certainty; a report established with certainty (thabat) as opposed to mere conjecture.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Certainty of knowledge (yaqīn) that fixes the heart; in legal contexts, an authenticated report that removes doubt.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: that which stands firm. Metaphorical: a chain of transmission so solid it cannot be shaken.
- Root: ز-ن-د-ق (z-n-d-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A Manichaean, heretic, one who conceals unbelief; the diminutive (zindīq) intensifies contempt.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): One whose outward conformity masks inward corruption of doctrine; a term of takfīr in theological polemics.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: follower of Zoroaster/Manes. Metaphorical: anyone whose learning breeds skepticism rather than submission.
- Root: ج-د-ل (j-d-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To twist, to braid tightly; disputation that interweaves arguments.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dialectical argumentation (jadal) — in the Qur'an, both praiseworthy (disputing with the People of the Book in the better way) and blameworthy (contending in falsehood).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: the twisting of ropes. Metaphorical: the twisting of speech in debate — here, blameworthy wrangling that exhausts the mind without yielding fruit.
- Sībawayh Rule: The Rule of the Conditional Clause with فاء (Fā' al-Sababiyyah) — When a conditional sentence is followed by a clause introduced by fa-, the fa- marks the apodosis as the necessary consequence of the protasis, as in "If you read knowledge in this way, then (fa-) you will emerge a zindīq."
translation:
Al-Māzarī said: I was once before my master in the discipline of uṣūl (legal theory); then the authenticated report (al-thabat) arrived that the day was from Ramaḍān. I said: "This day is not to be made up (qadā') according to the narration of Mālik and some of his companions." My master seized my ear and said to me: "If you read knowledge under this one, then do not read it — for you will emerge from it a zindīq," using this word in the diminutive form (taṣghīr) of zindīq. And some of them may be as Ibn Muḥriz said concerning the question of the overlapping of numbers (tadākhul al-ʿadad): "Whoever's intellect does not reach the comprehension of the meaning flees from the weariness of his thought to clinging to the outward appearance of disagreement." End quote. So consider: whoever's aspiration is in reading [for its own sake], what fruit will he have in the outward world, whether in a legal verdict (fatwā) or in worship? And knowledge is only for action; and there will come, in the discussion of this station concerning spiritual ascent (al-taraqqī), that it is not fitting for the one who is moderate in the pursuit of knowledge — let alone the one who races to good deeds — to immerse himself in disputation (jadal).

They said: A person is not obligated to know the substance (jawhar) and the accident (ʿaraḍ), for the Companions — may God be pleased with them — died without knowing them. Nor is he obligated to know whether the name is the named or other than it, nor the interpretation of the ḥadīths in which there occur the Face, the Hand, the Istiwā' (establishing upon the Throne), Speech, Descent, Vision, the Throne, Laughter, and the wiping of Adam's back; nor [the interpretation of] that {«Qul Huwa Allāhu Aḥad»} equals a third of the Qur'an. Nor will a person be asked on the Day of Resurrection about qaḍā' and qadar (divine decree). Nor is he obligated to know the ruling concerning children who died young, nor whether so-and-so is more virtuous than so-and-so even if he were a Companion, nor whether there are angels with the disbelievers, nor the ruling concerning Gog and Magog, nor whether the spirit (rūḥ) is an accident or a body, nor the modality of the seizing of the spirit, nor the argument of Adam with Moses, nor the Prophet's ﷺ seeing of Jesus and the Dajjāl, nor the meaning of "his reward is decreased by a qīrāṭ," nor the meaning of "the believer's soul is a bird," nor "the extent of the muezzin's voice," nor "the devil's knot upon the crown of the head," nor the modality of the devils' eating and drinking, nor the meaning of "the Qur'an was revealed upon seven letters," nor "the fornicator does not fornicate while he is a believer," nor the modality of the weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection, nor the difference between the poor person (faqīr) and the destitute person (miskīn), nor the meaning of "no harm and no reciprocating harm," nor "do not spy and do not eavesdrop," nor the meaning of al-Dhāriyāt and al-Mursalāt, nor when the Hour will come. Nor is he obligated to learn from the craft of grammar (naḥw) except that which leads to the understanding of how to speak correctly. And whatever is beyond that is superfluous — such as [the rules of] the raiser of the subject (rāfiʿ al-mubtada') and the accusative of the adverb as predicate (nāṣib al-ẓarf khabaran).

title_ar: وقد يكون للعالم في هذا المأخذ مقصد يصير ذلك كله له حسنة بنسب
title_en: On the Scholar's Intent in This Approach, Rendering All His Efforts a Virtue by Attribution
arabic_text:
وقد يكون للعالم في هذا المأخذ مقصد يصير ذلك كله له حسنة بنسبة كقول المازري: لما فرغ من الحكم على من نسي صلاة وثانيتها ونحو ذلك؛ قال: وإنما ذكرنا هذه المسائل ليكد الطالب فبها فهمه؛ فيكتسب من كده لقهمه فيها اتبامًا وتيقظا فيما سواها من المعاني الفقهبة وغيرها مما يطالعه. وقد قسم في "الإحياء” العلوم المحمودة: وأن منها علومًا ليست بشرعية كالطب والحساب: قال: وكلاهما فرض كفاية؛ لو خلا البلد عمن يقوم بذلك لحرج أهل البلد: وإذا قام بذلك أحد اسقط عن الباقين. قال: ولا تعجب من كون هذين من فروض الكفاية؛ فإن أصول الصتاعات من فروض الكفاية حتى الحجامة؛ لو خلا البلد من حجام لسارع الهلاك إليهم؛ وحرجوا بتعريضهم أنفسهم للهلاك؛ فإن الذي أنزل الداء أنزل الدواء؛ وأرشد إلى استعماله؛ وأعد الأسباب لتعاطيه: فلا يجوز التعرض للهلاك بإهماله. قال: وأما ما يعد فضيلة لا فريضة؛ فالتعمق في دقائق الحساب وخفايا الطب وغير ذلك مما يستغنى عنه» ولكن يفيد زيادة قوة في القدر المحتاج إليه. اه من “الإحياء". فانظر فإذا كان هذا التقسيم بالنسبة للعلوم غير الشرعية؛ من باب أولى للعلوم الشرعية من باب ما لا يتوصل للواجب إلا به فهو واجب.

وقد قال أيضًا في "الاحياء': وأما المباح من العلوم؛ فالعلم بالأشعار التي ل سخف فيها وتواريخ الأخبار وما يجري مجراهاء ومن نحو هذا قول الحافظ. أبي عمر في استذكاره قال: معرفة أعمار العلماء والوقوف على وفياتهم من علم خاصة أهل العلم؛ وأنه لا ينبغي من وسم بالعلم نفسه جهل ذلك؛ وإنه مما يلزمه من العلم العناية به والقيام بحفظه. وبالجملة فقد تيين بما قررته أن طلاب العلم كما / اينهم ع قال اله تعالى: ( َنم رقم 4917 والترمني (356/4: رقم 1988) وقال: حسن صحيح. ومالك (907/2: رقم 01616 وأحمد (287/2: رقم 7845)» وأخرجه أبضاء الطبراتي في الأوسط (22218 رقم 846 واليهقي 017لا رقم 03813 يَدَخُويهًا ...4 [فاطر: 33]ء وتقدم قول رسول الله يكة: وظالمنا مغفور له”": فنسآل الله العظيم أن يحقق لنا هذا الوعد الكريم؛ وأن يتفع البعض بالبعض: وأن يغفر لنا أجمعين؛ إنه أرحم الراحمين؛ ثم من دون هذا المقام مقام آخرا هو المقام السادس.
anchors:
- Root: ق-ص-د (qaṣada)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To aim, intend, or direct one's course toward a goal; the core sense is deliberate orientation of action.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In theological discourse, denotes intentionality (qaṣd) as the moral determinant of acts—what renders an act praiseworthy or blameworthy.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical direction toward a place; metaphorical: the soul's inclination toward an objective, here implying a noble purpose that transmutes means into ends.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional-Resultative Construction (al-sharṭ wa al-jawāb) — The clause "قد يكون... مقصد" establishes a possibility, followed by a result clause ("يصير...") governed by the antecedent's semantic scope, requiring careful tracking of pronominal referents (kull dhālika) across the periodic sentence.
translation:
I say: And it may be that the scholar, in this approach, has an intent by which all of that becomes for him a virtue by attribution—as in the saying of al-Māzarī: When he had finished adjudicating on the case of one who forgets a prayer and its second [occurrence] and the like thereof, he said: "We have only mentioned these questions to weary the student, so that through his weariness his understanding may be sharpened; and thus he acquires, from his toil, a firm grasp of them, and an alertness regarding what lies beyond them among the jurisprudential meanings and other matters he may encounter."

And he (al-Ghazālī) divided, in the "Iḥyā’," the praiseworthy sciences: and among them are sciences that are not religious—such as medicine and arithmetic. He said: "Both of these are a communal obligation (farḍ kifāyah); were a town to be emptied of one who undertakes them, the townspeople would fall into sin (ḥaraj). And when one person undertakes them, it is lifted from the rest." He said: "Do not marvel at these two being among the communal obligations; for the foundations of crafts are communal obligations—even cupping (ḥijāmah). Were a town devoid of a cupper, destruction would hasten upon them, and they would sin by exposing themselves to perdition. For He who sent down the malady sent down the remedy, guided to its use, and prepared the means for its application; so it is not permissible to expose oneself to destruction by neglecting it." He said: "As for what is counted a virtue and not an obligation—it is deep immersion in the subtleties of arithmetic, the hidden recesses of medicine, and the like of what is dispensable, yet it yields an increase of strength in that which is needed." End of quote from the "Iḥyā’."

So reflect: if this division holds for the non-religious sciences, then a fortiori (min bāb awlā) it applies to the religious sciences—under the principle that whatever leads to the obligatory is itself obligatory.

And he also said in the "Iḥyā’": "As for the permissible sciences—they are knowledge of poetry that contains no frivolity, and the chronicles of reports (tawārīkh al-akhbār), and what runs in their course." And of this kind is the saying of the ḥāfiẓ Abū ʿUmar in his "Istidhkār": "Knowledge of the ages of the scholars and ascertaining their death-dates belongs to the special knowledge of the people of learning; and it behooves not one who is branded with knowledge to be ignorant of that; rather, it is among the knowledge he is bound to tend to and preserve."

In sum, it has become clear by what I have established that the seekers of knowledge—as the saying of the Prophet ﷺ has come: "We are the later ones and the foremost on the Day of Resurrection" —and God the Exalted has said: {«وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَذْهَبَ عَنَّا الْحَزَنَ»} [Fāṭir: 34], and there has preceded the saying of the Messenger of God ﷺ: "And our wrongdoer is forgiven." So we ask God the Magnificent to realize for us this noble promise, to benefit some of us by others, and to forgive us all together; verily, He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. Then, below this station there is another station—and it is the sixth.
